title: Long-term stability and reproducibility of frozen plasma control samples for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, and human immunodeficiency virus by quantitative PCR: Implications for retrospective testing in hemovigilance.
abstract: Abstract Objective Data on the long‐term stability and reproducibility of nucleic acid amplification testing (NAT) results in frozen stored positive samples (≤−20°C) remain limited. This study evaluated the long‐term performance of frozen virus‐positive samples in quantitative PCR assays and aimed to provide evidence for their analytical reliability in retrospective NAT and quality assurance. Because blood transfusions, despite their high safety, still carry a residual risk of transmission of blood‐borne viruses, these data may also be relevant for look‐back investigations in hemovigilance. Materials and Methods Diluted and aliquoted internal run controls from positive patient samples were retrospectively analyzed using routine quantitative PCR assays. Long‐term stability was assessed over 37 months for HIV, 25 and 29 months for HBV‐A and HBV‐B, and 49 and 38 months for HCV‐A and HCV‐B. Descriptive statistics and linear regression were used to assess variability and temporal trends. Compliance with the German Medical Association's guidelines for quality assurance in medical laboratory testing (Rili‐BAEK) was evaluated using an acceptance range of ±0.5 log10. Results All internal run controls demonstrated stable long‐term performance during frozen storage and routine use. Across the datasets, 99.2%–100% of measurements remained within the acceptance range. Results outside mean ± 3 SD were rare, and no statistically significant temporal trend was observed for any internal run control. Conclusion Frozen HBV‐, HCV‐, and HIV‐positive samples showed robust long‐term stability and reproducibility in routine quantitative PCR assays for up to 4 years. These findings support the suitability of long‐term stored specimens for retrospective NAT.

title_zh: 冷冻血浆控制样本在乙型肝炎病毒、丙型肝炎病毒和人类免疫缺陷病毒定量PCR检测中的长期稳定性和可重复性:对输血安全监测中回顾性检测的启示。
source_body_en: Abstract Objective Data on the long‐term stability and reproducibility of nucleic acid amplification testing (NAT) results in frozen stored positive samples (≤−20°C) remain limited. This study evaluated the long‐term performance of frozen virus‐positive samples in quantitative PCR assays and aimed to provide evidence for their analytical reliability in retrospective NAT and quality assurance. Because blood transfusions, despite their high safety, still carry a residual risk of transmission of blood‐borne viruses, these data may also be relevant for look‐back investigations in hemovigilance. Materials and Methods Diluted and aliquoted internal run controls from positive patient samples were retrospectively analyzed using routine quantitative PCR assays. Long‐term stability was assessed over 37 months for HIV, 25 and 29 months for HBV‐A and HBV‐B, and 49 and 38 months for HCV‐A and HCV‐B. Descriptive statistics and linear regression were used to assess variability and temporal trends. Compliance with the German Medical Association's guidelines for quality assurance in medical laboratory testing (Rili‐BAEK) was evaluated using an acceptance range of ±0.5 log10. Results All internal run controls demonstrated stable long‐term performance during frozen storage and routine use. Across the datasets, 99.2%–100% of measurements remained within the acceptance range. Results outside mean ± 3 SD were rare, and no statistically significant temporal trend was observed for any internal run control. Conclusion Frozen HBV‐, HCV‐, and HIV‐positive samples showed robust long‐term stability and reproducibility in routine quantitative PCR assays for up to 4 years. These findings support the suitability of long‐term stored specimens for retrospective NAT.
abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 目前关于冷冻保存的阳性样本(≤−20°C)中核酸扩增检测(NAT)结果的长期稳定性和可重复性数据仍然有限。本研究评估了冷冻保存的病毒阳性样本在定量PCR检测中的长期性能,并旨在为其在回顾性NAT和质量保证中的分析可靠性提供证据。尽管血液输注具有较高的安全性,但仍存在血液传播病毒传播的残留风险,因此这些数据也可能对输血安全监测中的回顾性调查具有相关性。材料和方法 使用来自阳性患者样本的稀释和分装的内部运行控制样本,通过常规的定量PCR检测进行回顾性分析。长期稳定性评估分别在HIV样本上进行了37个月,在HBV-A和HBV-B样本上进行了25和29个月,在HCV-A和HCV-B样本上进行了49和38个月。使用描述性统计和线性回归来评估变异性和时间趋势。通过德国医学协会关于医疗实验室检测质量保证的指南(Rili-BAEK)的接受范围±0.5 log10来评估符合情况。结果 所有内部运行控制样本在冷冻保存和常规使用过程中均表现出稳定的长期性能。在所有数据集中,99.2%–100%的测量值均保持在接受范围内。测量值超出均值±3 SD的情况很少,且任何内部运行控制样本均未观察到统计学上显著的时间趋势。结论 冷冻保存的HBV、HCV和HIV阳性样本在常规定量PCR检测中表现出良好的长期稳定性和可重复性,最长可达4年。这些发现支持长期保存的样本用于回顾性NAT的适用性。

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

title: Associated factors of hepatitis B virus infection among pregnant women in Africa: an extension of a previous systematic review and meta-analysis on prevalence
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant public health concern among pregnant women in Africa. While previous reviews have focused on the prevalence of HBV, comprehensive evidence regarding the associated factors of HBV infection is limited. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify the associated factors of HBV infection in pregnant women in Africa. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Advanced Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library, and African Journal Online for observational studies published between July 18, 2013, and July 18, 2023. Studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for factors associated with HBV infection among pregnant women were included. We assessed methodological quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). We conducted separate random-effects meta-analyses using the DerSimonian–Laird method for each associated factor reported by at least two studies to estimate pooled adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Associated factors examined across multiple studies that differed substantially in exposure categories or reference groups were synthesized narratively. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Of the 19 included studies, 20 associated factors were eligible for the quantitative synthesis. Significant associations with HBV infection among pregnant women were a history of abortion (AOR = 3.08, 95% CI: 1.58–4.58), multiple sexual partners (AOR = 5.33, 95% CI: 2.50–8.17), blood transfusion (AOR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.38–3.90), hospital admission (AOR = 3.28, 95% CI: 2.02–4.53), surgery (AOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.04–3.92), HIV infection (AOR = 9.22, 95% CI: 2.39–16.05), tattooing (AOR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.26–3.80), female genital mutilation (AOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 2.02–2.94), dental procedures (AOR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.16–3,44), family history of HBV infection (AOR = 3.37, 95% CI: 1.94–4.80), contact with jaundiced patients (AOR = 4.18, 95% CI: 2.09–6.27), tonsillectomy (AOR = 4.87, 95% CI: 3.36–6.37), and sharing sharp materials (AOR = 2.87, 95% CI: 2.47–3.27). This meta-analysis identified multiple behavioral, medical, and household-related associated factors of HBV infection. Strengthening routine antenatal HBV screening, targeted risk assessment, vaccination strategies, and linkage-to-care interventions may help improve early detection and reduce mother-to-child transmission of HBV. PROSPERO 2025 CRD420251240694.

title: Hepatitis B Virus Knowledge, Preventive Practices, and Vaccination Status Among People Living with HIV at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research, Lagos: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) co-infection substantially increases liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLHIV). Although vaccination remains the most effective strategy for prevention HBV infection, its uptake is conventionally assumed to depend on adequate knowledge and positive attitudes towards vaccination. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HBV vaccination among HIV-positive patients and examined whether knowledge significantly predicts vaccination uptake. A cross-sectional institutional survey was conducted among 374 HIV-positive patients receiving care at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR), Yaba, Lagos State. Participants were selected using purposive sampling. and data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Data were analysed using SPSS version 26.0, through descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression with statistical significance set at p<0.05. The majority of respondents were female (70.2%), married (62.9%), and had tertiary-educated (40.7%). Overall, 82% of participants demonstrated low levels of knowledge regarding HBV infection and vaccination (Mean=1.20±0.443), while 58% exhibited negative attitudes toward HBV vaccination (Mean=2.73±0.580). Despite these findings, self-reported HBV vaccination uptake was relatively high (79.6%, Mean = 1.4\11±0.423). Healthcare facilities were identified as the primary source of HBV related information. Education level were significantly associated with vaccination status (p=0.025), while gender was significantly associated with knowledge level (p = 0.010). Occupation was not significantly associated with attitude (p = 0.466). Logistic regression analysis indicated that knowledge was not a significant predictor of vaccination uptake (χ2 = 4.49, p = 0.106, R2 = 0.018). The findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between knowledge and predominantly negative attitudes. This challenge the conventional assumption that knowledge necessarily drives vaccination behavior and suggest that health-system factors, including routine vaccine provision and health-care provider recommendations, may play a more important role in vaccination uptake among PLHIV. Interventions should therefore combine improved vaccine accessibility and provider-led vaccination strategies with targeted education, particularly through the integration of HBV vaccination into routine HIV care.

title_zh: HIV携带者中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)共感染在尼日利亚医学研究所拉各斯的肝相关发病率和死亡率:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) co-infection substantially increases liver-related morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (PLHIV). Although vaccination remains the most effective strategy for prevention HBV infection, its uptake is conventionally assumed to depend on adequate knowledge and positive attitudes towards vaccination. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HBV vaccination among HIV-positive patients and examined whether knowledge significantly predicts vaccination uptake. A cross-sectional institutional survey was conducted among 374 HIV-positive patients receiving care at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR), Yaba, Lagos State. Participants were selected using purposive sampling. and data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Data were analysed using SPSS version 26.0, through descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression with statistical significance set at p<0.05. The majority of respondents were female (70.2%), married (62.9%), and had tertiary-educated (40.7%). Overall, 82% of participants demonstrated low levels of knowledge regarding HBV infection and vaccination (Mean=1.20±0.443), while 58% exhibited negative attitudes toward HBV vaccination (Mean=2.73±0.580). Despite these findings, self-reported HBV vaccination uptake was relatively high (79.6%, Mean = 1.4\11±0.423). Healthcare facilities were identified as the primary source of HBV related information. Education level were significantly associated with vaccination status (p=0.025), while gender was significantly associated with knowledge level (p = 0.010). Occupation was not significantly associated with attitude (p = 0.466). Logistic regression analysis indicated that knowledge was not a significant predictor of vaccination uptake (χ2 = 4.49, p = 0.106, R2 = 0.018). The findings demonstrate a notable disconnect between knowledge and predominantly negative attitudes. This challenge the conventional assumption that knowledge necessarily drives vaccination behavior and suggest that health-system factors, including routine vaccine provision and health-care provider recommendations, may play a more important role in vaccination uptake among PLHIV. Interventions should therefore combine improved vaccine accessibility and provider-led vaccination strategies with targeted education, particularly through the integration of HBV vaccination into routine HIV care.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)共感染显著增加了HIV携带者(PLHIV)的肝相关发病率和死亡率。尽管疫苗接种仍然是预防HBV感染最有效的策略,但其普及率通常被认为取决于对疫苗接种的充分知识和积极态度。本研究评估了HIV阳性患者对HBV疫苗接种的知识、态度和行为,并探讨了知识是否显著预测疫苗接种的普及率。在尼日利亚医学研究所(NIMR)位于拉各斯州亚巴的机构中,对374名接受HIV治疗的患者进行了横断面调查。参与者通过目的抽样法选取,数据通过结构化问卷收集。数据使用SPSS 26.0版本进行分析,包括描述性统计、卡方检验和逻辑回归分析,统计学显著性设定为p<0.05。大多数受访者为女性(70.2%),已婚(62.9%),拥有高等教育背景(40.7%)。总体而言,82%的参与者对HBV感染和疫苗接种的知识水平较低(均值=1.20±0.443),而58%的受访者对HBV疫苗接种表现出负面态度(均值=2.73±0.580)。尽管如此,自我报告的HBV疫苗接种普及率相对较高(79.6%,均值=1.4\11±0.423)。医疗设施被确认为HBV相关信息的主要来源。教育水平与疫苗接种状态显著相关(p=0.025),而性别与知识水平显著相关(p=0.010)。职业与态度无显著相关性(p=0.466)。逻辑回归分析表明,知识不是疫苗接种普及率的显著预测因素(χ2=4.49,p=0.106,R2=0.018)。研究结果表明,知识与主要负面态度之间存在显著脱节。这挑战了传统假设,即知识必然驱动疫苗接种行为,并表明健康系统因素,包括常规抗病毒药物的提供和医疗保健提供者的建议,可能在HIV携带者中对疫苗接种普及率发挥更重要的作用。因此,干预措施应结合改善抗病毒药物的可及性、以医疗保健提供者为主导的疫苗接种策略以及有针对性的教育,特别是在将HBV疫苗接种纳入常规HIV护理中时。

title: Point of Care Diagnostics for Hepatitis B and C in Low-resource Settings: A Narrative Review
abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) continue to be major public health challenge especially in Low- and MiddleIncome Countries (LMICs), with poor laboratory capacity and the ability to detect the disease earlier and contribute to its management. Proper and timely diagnosis is crucial for clinical intervention and global elimination. The present narrative review explores the potential for the use of Point-Of-Care (POC) testing to enhance the testing of HBV and HCV in low-resource settings. title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B.
abstract: Approved chronic hepatitis B therapies rarely result in functional cure, as they fail to permanently silence all transcriptionally active hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA. CRMA-1001 employs an optimized epigenetic silencer that represses viral transcription through targeted deposition of DNA methylation on episomal and integrated HBV DNAs. Here we showed that in HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 produced >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, which correlated with de novo methylation of HBV DNA. Three doses resulted in up to 90% of animals with undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post treatment. In non-human primates, CRMA-1001 induced transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested. Expression and DNA methylation profiling revealed no detectable unintended targets in the human genome. These findings support the initiation of clinical development of CRMA-1001 as a finite treatment course with the potential for functional cure in individuals living with chronic hepatitis B. A nanomedicine comprising a guide RNA and an mRNA co-encapsulated in a lipid nanoparticle for delivery to hepatocytes holds promise for a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B through epigenetic silencing.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the limitations of current hepatitis B virus (HBV) therapies, which rarely achieve a functional cure by failing to silence all transcriptionally active HBV DNA. The research focused on CRMA-1001, an epigenetic silencer designed to repress viral transcription through DNA methylation. In HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 led to >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, with three doses achieving up to 90% undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post-treatment. In non-human primates, the therapy caused transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested, and no unintended targets were detected in the human genome. These results suggest that CRMA-1001 could be a promising finite treatment for chronic HBV, potentially leading to a functional cure. However, the study's findings are based on animal models, and further clinical trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety in humans.

source_body_en: Approved chronic hepatitis B therapies rarely result in functional cure, as they fail to permanently silence all transcriptionally active hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA. CRMA-1001 employs an optimized epigenetic silencer that represses viral transcription through targeted deposition of DNA methylation on episomal and integrated HBV DNAs. Here we showed that in HBV mouse models, a single dose of CRMA-1001 produced >3-log10 reductions in viral biomarkers, which correlated with de novo methylation of HBV DNA. Three doses resulted in up to 90% of animals with undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen and HBV DNA by 6 months post treatment. In non-human primates, CRMA-1001 induced transient liver transaminase elevations only at the highest dose tested. Expression and DNA methylation profiling revealed no detectable unintended targets in the human genome. These findings support the initiation of clinical development of CRMA-1001 as a finite treatment course with the potential for functional cure in individuals living with chronic hepatitis B. A nanomedicine comprising a guide RNA and an mRNA co-encapsulated in a lipid nanoparticle for delivery to hepatocytes holds promise for a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B through epigenetic silencing.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 批准的慢性乙型肝炎疗法很少能实现功能性治愈,因为它们无法永久沉默所有转录活跃的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)DNA。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: CRMA-1001采用了一种优化的表观遗传沉默剂,通过在环状和整合的HBV DNA上靶向沉积DNA甲基化来抑制病毒转录。
analysis_zh.main_results: 三次剂量后,6个月治疗后,高达90%的动物检测不到乙型肝炎表面抗原和HBV DNA。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在非人灵长类动物中,CRMA-1001仅在最高剂量测试时诱导了短暂的肝转氨酶升高。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 表达和DNA甲基化分析显示,在人类基因组中未检测到可识别的意外靶点。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些发现支持启动CRMA-1001的临床开发,作为一种有限的治疗疗程,可能在与慢性乙型肝炎共存的个体中实现功能性治愈。

media_mentions.title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B - Nature
media_mentions.rss_summary_html: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B  Nature
media_mentions.excerpt_original: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B Nature
media_mentions.priority_tier_reason: 新闻聚合或正文证据有限，作为补充信息
media_mentions.content_title: Development of an investigational epigenetic silencer therapy to transcriptionally inactivate viral DNA in chronic hepatitis B - Nature Biomedical Engineering
media_mentions.content: Ethics statement All studies involving the use of animals were conducted in compliance with animal care and use protocols approved by institutional animal care and use committees (IACUC) of corresponding testing facilities: Wuxi Apptec, nChroma Bio and AltaSciences. The health assessment of animals was performed in accordance with IACUC standard operating procedures and guidelines of each testing facility. In silico HBV conservation and gRNA designs Guide target conservation analysis was performed by assessing exact matches between the target sequence including presence of the dSpCas9 NGG PAM and the reference genomes with A–E genotypes found in HBVdb21 using NCBI BLAST40. The percentage of exact matches per genotype was used to assess conservation. RNA production Using standard methods by commercial suppliers, 100-mer gRNAs were chemically synthesized. The gRNAs used for in vitro screens contain 2′-O-methylation and phosphorothioate linkages at the three terminal nucleotides of both the 5′ and 3′ ends, as previously described15. Subsequent studies in vitro and in vivo employed gRNAs containing both end-modifications as well as a proprietary pattern of 2′-O-methylation throughout the sequence. All gRNA target sequence used in this study are presented in Supplementary Table 1. mRNA was produced via in vitro transcription and purification. Plasmids containing an epigenetic silencer or a control construct were linearized by restriction digest and used as a template with T7 RNA polymerase, NTPs (including N1-methylpseudouridine) and cap analogue. mRNAs either underwent enzymatic A-tailing or contained an encoded polyA in the template, as previously described15. The amino acid sequences of all constructs used in these studies are presented in Supplementary Table 2. LNP formulations Small-scale LNP formulations of epigenetic silencer mRNA and gRNA for screens and initial HepG2.2.15 studies were prepared using GenVoy-ILM kits. Formulations were optimized with an aim to attain LNPs of uniform size and high encapsulation efficiency. The ratio of lipids to the total RNA cargo, comprising mRNA and gRNA, was calculated on the basis of the molar weights of lipids and RNAs. Medium-scale LNP formulations used in in vitro, rodent and NHP studies contained an ionizable cationic lipid proprietary to Acuitas Therapeutics, as well as phosphatidylcholine/cholesterol/PEG-lipid. The proprietary lipid and LNP compositions are described in patent application WO2020146805A1. The RNAs were mixed and encapsulated in LNP using a self-assembly process as described previously15,41. The resulting LNPs had a diameter ≤70 nm as measured by dynamic light scattering using a Zetasizer Nano ZS (Malvern Instruments) instrument and encapsulation efficiencies of more than 97% as measured by Quant-iT RiboGreen Assay (Life Technologies). In vitro studies HepG2.2.15 and PLC/PRF/5 cell culture and treatment HepG2.2.15 cells were cultured in DMEM (Gibco, 11965092) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Gibco, A5670501) and 1% penicillin–streptomycin (Gibco, 15140122). A day before treatment, 20,000 cells per well were seeded in collagen type I-coated 96-well plates. On the following day, the cells were treated with 100 μl of fresh medium supplemented with LNP-formulated epigenetic silencers at a single dose of 0.5 μg ml−1 or an 8-point serial dilution (4–0.031 μg ml−1) and/or 1 μg ml−1 of recombinant human apolipoprotein E3 (rhApoE3) (a supplement to facilitate LNP transfection in cell culture), also referred to as mock treatment. Plates were maintained and subcultured (cell trypsinization every 3–4 days), and supernatants or cell samples were collected at various time points from 6 h to 27 days after treatment and stored at −80 °C until analysis. Studies to evaluate EE protein were performed in 24-well plate format, and 118,750 cells per well were seeded and treatment with 500 μl of fresh medium supplemented with 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and or 1 μg ml−1 of CRMA-1001. PLC/PRF/5 cells (ATCC, CRL-8024) were cultured in Eagle’s minimum essential medium (Corning, 10-009-CV) with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin–streptomycin and maintained as described above for 96-well plates. Cells were treated with 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 (mock-treatment control) and/or 1 μg ml−1 of CRMA-1001, then supernatants were collected at 7 and 14 days after treatment and stored at −80 °C until analysis. PHH cell culture, infection and treatment PHHs isolated from humanized mouse liver (PXB-cells) (PhoenixBio)42 were received pre-plated in 24-well plates and maintained in culture medium (dHCGM medium (PhoenixBio) and 10% FBS) and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO 2 . To establish HBV infection, 4 days before treatment, HBV was diluted in infection medium (dHCGM, 10% FBS, 4% PEG8000 and and 2.5% DMSO) at a multiplicity of genome equivalents (MGE) of 2,000 per cell of HBV genotype D (Imquest BioSciences). The supernatant was collected from all wells and replaced with infection medium. The following day, 16 h after infection, the medium was removed, cells were washed twice with Dulbecco’s phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) and 500 μl of fresh maintenance medium (dHCGM, 10% FBS and 2.5% DMSO) was added to each well. For studies with uninfected PHHs, cells were maintained in culture medium upon treatment. On the day of treatment (day 0), PHHs were treated with 500 μl culture medium supplemented with 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and 0.5 or 1 μg ml−1 CRMA-1001 or rhApoE3 only (mock-treatment control). At 14 days post treatment, the supernatants were collected, cells washed and both stored at −80 °C until analysis. Primary HSECs and primary HAdCC treatment Primary HSECs (Innoprot and Accegen) from three different human donors were cultured in medium (endothelial cell medium (ScienCell) with 5% FBS, 1% penicillin–streptomycin and 1% endothelial cell growth supplement (ScienCell)) and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO 2 . A day before test or control article treatment, 10,000 cells per well were seeded into a 96-well tissue culture plate precoated with 150 μg ml−1 of human fibronectin and containing 200 μl culture medium. On the day of treatment (day 0), culture medium was replaced with 100 μl of fresh medium containing 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and CRMA-1001 or control articles. On day 14, the cells were washed with 200 μl DPBS per well, lysed with 63 μl Beckman Coulter Buffer LBE with Proteinase K, incubated for 30 min at room temperature and frozen at −80 °C in plate format. Primary HAdCCs (Accegen) were cultured in medium (Mesenchymal Stem Cell Medium (Innoprot) with 5% FBS, 1% penicillin–streptomycin and 1% Mesenchymal Stem Cell Growth Serum (Innoprot)) and incubated at 37 °C and 5% CO 2 . A day before test or control article treatment, 10,000 cells per well were seeded into a 96-well tissue culture plate precoated with 150 μg ml−1 of poly-l-lysine (Sigma-Aldrich) and containing 200 μl culture medium. On the day of treatment (day 0), the culture medium was replaced with 100 μl of medium containing 1 μg ml−1 of rhApoE3 and CRMA-1001 or control articles. The plates were maintained and cells subcultured (cell trypsinization every 3–4 days, followed by transfer of ~10,000 cells to a new 96-well culture plate with fresh medium). On day 14, cells were washed with 200 μl DPBS per well, lysed with 63 μl Beckman Coulter Buffer LBE with Proteinase K, incubated for 30 min at room temperature and frozen at −80 °C in plate format. Cell viability assays Viability was assessed using Cell Titer-Glo (Promega, G924B) or Cell Titer-Blue Assays (Promega, G8080) according to the manufacturer’s recommendations. The fluorescent signal obtained was measured using the Infinite 200 PRO Microplate Reader with a 560Ex/590Em filter set (TECAN). To account for technical variability in cell number during subculture, the secreted antigen concentrations were normalized to cell viability in each individual well and expressed as a percentage relative to control-treated cells. Primary screening in vitro in HepG2-NTCP cells For the initial screening experiments, EEs were delivered to HepG2-NTCP cells as three individual mRNAs, each encoding an engineered transcriptional repressor as previously described43 (dCas9-KRAB mRNA, DNMT3A mRNA and DNMT3L mRNA) as well as the candidate single guide RNA mixed at a 1:1:1:4 ratio. The RNA mix was formulated into LNPs using the Genvoy-ILM Lipid Mix kit (Precision Nanosystems). The HepG2-NTCP cell line was generated using HepG2 cells acquired from ATCC and transduced with a lentiviral vector to stably express the NTCP receptor. Cells were maintained in DMEM (Gibco, 21969035) supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% of glutamine and 1% penicillin–streptomycin. HepG2-NTCP cells were plated at 20,000 cells per well in collagen-coated 96-well plates and infected 24 h later with HBV genotype D at 5,000 MGE using DMEM medium supplemented with 4% PEG8000 and 2.5% DMSO. At 16 h post infection, the medium was removed, and the cells were washed with PBS and maintained in DMEM medium supplemented with 2.5% DMSO. Subsequently, 4 days after infection, the cells were treated with LNPs, and the medium was changed 1 and 3 days after LNP treatment. Finally, the supernatant was collected 6 days after transfection, and HBeAg and HBsAg levels were quantified by ELISA (Dia.Pro) and cell viability by Cell Titer-Blue Assay. HBV infection and the antiviral effect of treatments was analysed by HBeAg/HBsAg quantification. Guide potency was assessed by normalizing HBsAg and HBeAg measurement for each guide by the cell viability value for that guide. All animals were acclimated for 10 days during which the baseline levels of circulating HBV biomarkers (HBsAg, HBV DNA, and HBeAg) were measured. On day 0, all animals received a single i.v. bolus administration of vehicle, HBV-EE4000 (0.5, 1 and 3 mg kg−1) or CRMA-1001 (0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 mg kg−1). Peripheral blood samples were collected for biomarker analysis. At the end of study, all animals were euthanized, and liver samples were collected for further molecular assessment. Male C57BL/6J mice (6–8 weeks old) were obtained from The Jackson Laboratory. Circulating HBsAg levels were assessed at 2, 3 and 4 weeks post transduction to establish baseline levels and determine eligibility for study enrollment. Mice with mean baseline HBsAg levels between 5,000 IU ml−1 and 50,000 IU ml−1 were included. Animals meeting this criterion were randomized into treatment groups, with the goal of achieving an average baseline HBsAg level of approximately 10,000 IU ml−1 per group. Eligible animals were further treated with either vehicle or CRMA-1001 (0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 mg kg−1). In the combination treatment group, CRMA-1001 (0.5 mg kg−1) was administered in conjunction with ETV (Sigma, SML110), which was delivered via daily oral gavage at 0.01 mg kg−1 for 28 days. Fresh ETV dosing solutions (diluted in saline) were prepared weekly. Peripheral blood samples were collected for biomarker analysis throughout the study. At the end of the study, all animals were euthanized, and liver tissues were collected for molecular analyses. The PK and biodistribution studies consisted of male and female animal monkeys randomized into two groups of one to six animals per sex per group. Groups received a single i.v. infusion over 1 h of vehicle (n = 3) (0.9% sodium chloride) or CRMA-1001 at 2 mg kg−1 (n = 16). Animals were euthanized at 1 h, 24 h, 7 days and 28 days post infusion to assess PKs and biodistribution of CRMA-1001. The Good Laboratory Practice toxicity study consisted of male and female naive monkeys randomized into four groups of three to five animals per sex per group. Groups received three i.v. infusions for 1 h of vehicle (n = 8) (0.9% sodium chloride), or CRMA-1001 at dose levels of 0.5 mg kg−1 (n = 6), 1 mg kg−1 (n = 10) or 2 mg kg−1 (n = 10), every 4 weeks. Animals were fasted for at least 4 h before serum chemistry collections with access to water. Blood was collected from a peripheral vein, and serum was obtained for clinical chemistry analyses using a clinical analyzer. Serum chemistry, including ALT, AST and TBIL, was monitored at baseline and through the duration of the study, up to 4 weeks following the last CRMA-1001 dose administration. For the ionizable lipid analysis, monkey plasma samples were processed using a protein precipitation procedure. The extracts were analysed by HPLC with detection by tandem mass spectrometry. The mobile phase was nebulized using heated nitrogen set to TurboSpray positive ionization mode and the compounds were detected using tandem mass spectrometry. For biodistribution studies, tissue RNA was extracted using QIAGEN QIAcube HT kits, and an RT–ddPCR assay for the effector mRNA was performed using the primers described above. In addition, biodistribution of CRMA-1001 was evaluated using an RNAscope ISH assay for detection of the Cas9 portion of the EE mRNA in tissues. Selected monkey tissues were formalin-fixed according to a protocol provided by Advanced Cell Diagnostics (Biotechne). title: Molecular Evolution of Hepatitis B Virus in India: Insights into Genotype Diversity and Recombination
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a major public health problem in India, with considerable genetic variability arising out of evolutionary selection pressure, recombination events and reverse-transcription stage in its life cycle. This affects the transmission patterns, disease chronicity, and treatment response of the virus. Although HBV genotypes A, C, and D have been described in India, detailed whole-genome sequence data are scarce. Methods Residual HBsAg positive samples (n = 1963), received for inter-laboratory quality control or for referral diagnostic testing between 2006 and 2023 were screened, and n = 172 of these were positive for HBV DNA by realtime PCR. HBV DNA positive samples with high viral load (n = 32), collected from nine states of India, were used for whole-genome sequencing. DNA extracted these serum samples was subjected to whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on the Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) MinION platform. Genotype-specific tiled amplicons (~ 1000 bp) were used for library preparation. Consensus genomes were assembled, genotyped, and phylogenetically analysed using MEGA v11.0. Recombinant sequences were characterized further by SimPlot v3.5.1 boot scanning and confirmed with χ2 testing of phylogenetically informative sites. Results HBV genotype D (70.96%) was found to be common genotype in several Indian states, with genotype A (3.22%) present in central and southern states and genotype C (6.45%) in the northeast. Notably, five samples showed evidence of recombination events, including genotypes A, C, and D. There were two recombinants in West Bengal, and one each in Chhattisgarh, Assam, and Maharashtra. SimPlot analysis of representative isolates showed clearly demarcated recombination breakpoints. Phylogenetic reconstruction also attested to the mosaic character of these genomes. Conclusions The present study emphasizes the genetic heterogeneity and evolutionary dynamics of HBV in India, and recombination as a key mechanism adding to viral diversity. The success in utilizing ONT for WGS of HBV directly from serum samples illustrates its utility for scalable genomic surveillance. The initiation of a nationwide HBV sequencing program will be pivotal in tracking emerging variants, informing therapeutic interventions, and facilitating India's role in the global HBV elimination drive.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular evolution of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) in India, focusing on genotype diversity and recombination. The research highlights the genetic variability of HBV due to evolutionary pressures and recombination events, which influence transmission patterns, disease chronicity, and treatment response. Whole-genome sequencing of 32 HBV DNA positive samples from nine Indian states revealed genotype D as the most prevalent, followed by A and C. Five samples showed evidence of recombination, with clearly demarcated breakpoints identified through SimPlot analysis. The study underscores the importance of genomic surveillance in tracking HBV variants and informing public health strategies. The use of Oxford Nanopore Technology for direct sequencing from serum samples demonstrates its potential for scalable monitoring. The findings emphasize the need for a nationwide HBV sequencing program to support global elimination efforts.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)是印度的主要公共卫生问题,其显著的遗传变异源于进化选择压力、重组事件以及其生命周期中的逆转录阶段。这影响了病毒的基因组模式、慢性化程度以及免疫应答。尽管在印度已描述了HBV基因型A、C和D,但详细的全基因组序列数据仍然稀缺。方法 从2006年至2023年间接收用于实验室间质量控制或转诊诊断测试的HBsAg阳性残留样本(n = 1963)中筛选,其中n = 172份样本通过实时PCR检测出HBV DNA阳性。从印度九个州收集的HBV DNA阳性样本中,病毒载量高的n = 32份样本用于全基因组测序。从这些血清样本中提取的DNA在Oxford Nanopore Technology(ONT)MinION平台上进行全基因组测序(WGS)。使用基因型特异性拼接扩增子(约1000 bp)进行文库制备。使用MEGA v11.0软件组装、基因型鉴定并进行系统发育分析。进一步通过SimPlot v3.5.1的boot扫描分析重组序列,并通过系统发育信息位点的χ2检验进行确认。结果 在多个印度州中,HBV基因型D(70.96%)是最常见的基因型,基因型A(3.22%)存在于中部和南部州,基因型C(6.45%)则分布在东北部。值得注意的是,有五份样本显示出重组事件的证据,包括基因型A、C和D。在西孟加拉邦发现了两份重组样本,在恰特泰斯加尔邦、阿萨姆邦和马哈拉施特拉邦各发现一份。对代表性分离株的SimPlot分析清楚地显示了重组断点。系统发育重建也证实了这些基因组的镶嵌特性。结论 本研究强调了印度HBV的遗传异质性和进化动态,并指出重组是增加病毒多样性的关键机制。利用ONT平台直接从血清样本中进行HBV全基因组测序的成功经验,展示了其在可扩展基因组监测中的应用价值。启动全国范围的HBV测序计划对于追踪新兴变异株、指导治疗干预以及促进印度在全球HBV消除行动中的作用至关重要。

title: Determinants of Adult Hepatitis B Vaccine Uptake in a High-Endemic Setting
abstract: Abstract Background Adult hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination remains a critical yet underutilized component of viral hepatitis prevention in many high-endemic settings. Although infant HBV vaccination has been widely integrated into national immunization programmes, adult vaccination often depends on individual awareness, healthcare access, and provider recommendation. Community-based evidence on the determinants of adult HBV vaccine uptake is needed to inform adult immunization strategies in resource-constrained settings. Objective To examine the individual- and health-system level factors associated with adult HBV vaccine uptake in a community-based population in a high-endemic setting and identify priorities for strengthening adult vaccination programmes. Methods We conducted a community-based cross-sectional survey among adults in Minna, Nigeria, using multistage sampling. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, HBV-related knowledge, healthcare access, and vaccination status were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to identify factors independently associated with vaccine uptake, with adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Results Among 426 participants, 167 (39.2%) had received at least one dose of HBV vaccine, and 38.5% had completed the vaccination series. abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在许多高流行地区,成人乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)疫苗接种仍然是病毒性肝炎预防中关键但未被充分利用的组成部分。尽管婴儿HBV疫苗接种已被广泛纳入国家免疫计划,但成人疫苗接种往往依赖于个人意识、医疗保健可及性和医疗提供者的推荐。需要基于社区的证据来了解成人HBV疫苗接种的影响因素,以指导资源匮乏地区的成人疫苗接种策略。目的 在高流行地区的社区人群中,探讨与成人HBV疫苗接种率相关的个体及卫生系统层面的因素,并确定加强成人疫苗接种计划的优先事项。方法 我们在尼日利亚Minna市对成人进行了基于社区的横断面调查,采用多阶段抽样方法。通过访谈员填写的问卷收集了有关社会人口学特征、HBV相关知识、医疗保健可及性以及疫苗接种状态的数据。使用带有稳健方差估计的修改泊松回归分析来确定与疫苗接种独立相关的因素,并报告了调整后的比值比(aPRs)和95%置信区间(CIs)。结果 在426名参与者中,167人(39.2%)至少接种过一剂HBV疫苗,38.5%的人完成了疫苗接种系列。在双变量分析中,疫苗接种与教育程度、职业、居住类型、选区、宗教信仰、HBV知识和医疗工作者推荐显著相关(所有p值均<0.05)。解释与创新性 本研究强调了社会人口学和卫生系统因素在影响成人HBV疫苗接种中的重要性,为改善高流行地区的疫苗接种策略提供了可操作的见解。科学与公共卫生意义 这些发现可以用于制定有针对性的干预措施,以提高成人HBV疫苗接种率,特别是在资源匮乏地区,医疗工作者的推荐和个人意识在疫苗接种中起着关键作用。局限性与证据强度 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法确定因果关系,且可能存在与自我报告数据相关的偏倚。由于研究的观察性质和缺乏纵向随访,证据强度中等。

title: Intradermal hepatitis B vaccination with or without Imiquimod in cirrhosis after prior vaccine nonresponse: A Randomised Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with cirrhosis show impaired immune responses to standard intramuscular (IM) hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, resulting in low seroconversion rates. Intradermal (ID) vaccination and topical imiquimod have been proposed as strategies to enhance vaccine immunogenicity. We conducted a randomized controlled pilot trial to compare three HBV revaccination strategies in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) who previously failed standard IM vaccination: IM revaccination, ID revaccination, and ID revaccination combined with imiquimod (ID+IMQ). The primary endpoint was seroconversion at Month 7, defined as anti-HBs titres ≥10 mIU/mL. METHODS: This monocentric, prospective study included 59 patients with ACLD and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL after prior HBV vaccination. Patients were randomized (1:1:1) to receive either IM vaccination (n=19; Engerix-B® 20 μg IM at Months 0, 1 and 6), ID vaccination (n=19; two 10 μg ID injections at the same time points), or ID vaccination preceded by topical imiquimod 5% application (n=21). RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, seroprotection rates at month 7 were 36.8% in the IM group, 84.2% in the ID group, and 66.7% in the ID+IMQ group (p<0.01). After Bonferroni correction, only the ID versus IM comparison remained statistically significant (p=0.003). Geometric mean anti-HBs titres were significantly higher in the ID (116 mIU/mL) and ID+IMQ (107 mIU/mL) groups compared with the IM group (12 mIU/mL) (p=0.004). No severe vaccine-related adverse reactions were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Intradermal HBV revaccination significantly improves seroconversion in non-responder patients with ACLD compared with IM vaccination, without additional benefit from imiquimod. These results support further evaluation of intradermal vaccination without imiquimod in a phase 3 trial. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: The study protocol has been registered before the patients' recruitment, in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT) of the European Medicine Agency (2021-000644-22), as well as on ClinicalTrials.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of intradermal (ID) hepatitis B vaccination, with or without imiquimod, in patients with cirrhosis who previously failed standard intramuscular (IM) vaccination. A randomized controlled pilot trial was conducted with 59 patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL. title_zh: 肝硬化患者在先前标准肌内接种乙型肝炎疫苗失败后,采用皮内接种乙型肝炎疫苗(含或不含咪喹莫特):一项随机试验。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with cirrhosis show impaired immune responses to standard intramuscular (IM) hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination, resulting in low seroconversion rates. Intradermal (ID) vaccination and topical imiquimod have been proposed as strategies to enhance vaccine immunogenicity. We conducted a randomized controlled pilot trial to compare three HBV revaccination strategies in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) who previously failed standard IM vaccination: IM revaccination, ID revaccination, and ID revaccination combined with imiquimod (ID+IMQ). The primary endpoint was seroconversion at Month 7, defined as anti-HBs titres ≥10 mIU/mL. METHODS: This monocentric, prospective study included 59 patients with ACLD and anti-HBs titres <10 mIU/mL after prior HBV vaccination. Patients were randomized (1:1:1) to receive either IM vaccination (n=19; Engerix-B® 20 μg IM at Months 0, 1 and 6), ID vaccination (n=19; two 10 μg ID injections at the same time points), or ID vaccination preceded by topical imiquimod 5% application (n=21). RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis, seroprotection rates at month 7 were 36.8% in the IM group, 84.2% in the ID group, and 66.7% in the ID+IMQ group (p<0.01). After Bonferroni correction, only the ID versus IM comparison remained statistically significant (p=0.003). Geometric mean anti-HBs titres were significantly higher in the ID (116 mIU/mL) and ID+IMQ (107 mIU/mL) groups compared with the IM group (12 mIU/mL) (p=0.004). No severe vaccine-related adverse reactions were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Intradermal HBV revaccination significantly improves seroconversion in non-responder patients with ACLD compared with IM vaccination, without additional benefit from imiquimod. These results support further evaluation of intradermal vaccination without imiquimod in a phase 3 trial. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: The study protocol has been registered before the patients' recruitment, in the European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT) of the European Medicine Agency (2021-000644-22), as well as on ClinicalTrials.

title: Effectiveness of Radio Messages in Reducing Public Hesitancy Toward Hepatitis B Vaccination in Selected North-Central States of Nigeria
abstract: Hepatitis B remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with low vaccination uptake exacerbated by widespread public hesitancy fueled by misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information, particularly in the North-Central states. Addressing this challenge necessitates effective health communication strategies capable of improving awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance. This study examined the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination, guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior, which was adopted due to its emphasis on understanding how attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control influence intention and health-related decision-making. Employing a survey research design, data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states, complemented by secondary data obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies. Findings revealed that the effectiveness of radio messages was significantly undermined by ineffective message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, limiting knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. Additionally, radio’s potential as a health communication tool was constrained by infrastructural limitations, diverse audience characteristics, linguistic barriers, inadequate programming strategies, and insufficient community engagement, all of which diminished message reach, relevance, and influence on vaccination decisions. The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear, and that radio stations and health authorities address infrastructural and audience-related challenges by expanding coverage to remote areas, incorporating multiple local languages, and adopting engaging programming strategies such as interactive talk shows and testimonials to enhance public receptivity and uptake of Hepatitis B vaccination.

source_records.title: Effectiveness of Radio Messages in Reducing Public Hesitancy Toward Hepatitis B Vaccination in Selected North-Central States of Nigeria
source_records.abstract: Hepatitis B remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with low vaccination uptake exacerbated by widespread public hesitancy fueled by misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information, particularly in the North-Central states. Addressing this challenge necessitates effective health communication strategies capable of improving awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance. This study examined the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination, guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior, which was adopted due to its emphasis on understanding how attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control influence intention and health-related decision-making. Employing a survey research design, data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states, complemented by secondary data obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies. Findings revealed that the effectiveness of radio messages was significantly undermined by ineffective message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, limiting knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. Additionally, radio’s potential as a health communication tool was constrained by infrastructural limitations, diverse audience characteristics, linguistic barriers, inadequate programming strategies, and insufficient community engagement, all of which diminished message reach, relevance, and influence on vaccination decisions. The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear, and that radio stations and health authorities address infrastructural and audience-related challenges by expanding coverage to remote areas, incorporating multiple local languages, and adopting engaging programming strategies such as interactive talk shows and testimonials to enhance public receptivity and uptake of Hepatitis B vaccination.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination in selected North-Central states of Nigeria. The central question is whether radio messages can improve awareness, trust, and vaccine acceptance among the population, particularly in the context of misinformation, cultural misconceptions, and limited access to reliable health information.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a survey research design, collecting data through structured questionnaires administered to residents in selected states. Secondary data were obtained from radio program archives and public health reports. Questionnaire responses were analyzed using simple percentages to quantify trends in perception, knowledge, and behavior, while secondary data underwent qualitative content analysis to assess message framing, cultural relevance, and persuasive strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that radio messages were ineffective in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination due to poor message design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content. These factors limited knowledge acquisition, trust building, and fear reduction, thereby sustaining vaccine hesitancy. The findings suggest that radio as a health communication tool has significant limitations in the context of Hepatitis B vaccination in the North-Central states of Nigeria.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights the limitations of radio messages in addressing public hesitancy, but it does not provide comparative data with other communication strategies. There is no mention of how the effectiveness of radio messages might vary across different demographic groups or how other factors such as socioeconomic status or education level might influence vaccine acceptance. The evidence also lacks information on the long-term impact of radio messages on vaccination behavior.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study recommends that radio messages be carefully evaluated and redesigned to ensure cultural relevance, clarity, and persuasive content that builds trust and reduces fear. analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the effectiveness of radio messages in reducing public hesitancy toward Hepatitis B vaccination in selected North-Central states of Nigeria. The study found that radio messages were ineffective due to poor design, cultural misalignment, and weak persuasive content, which limited knowledge acquisition and trust building. The review highlights the need for careful evaluation and redesign of radio messages to ensure cultural relevance and clarity, as well as addressing infrastructural and audience-related challenges to improve vaccine uptake. The findings suggest that radio, while a potential health communication tool, requires strategic improvements to be effective in this context.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究聚焦于在尼日利亚北中部部分州通过广播信息减少公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种犹豫态度的效果。核心问题是广播信息是否能够提高公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的意识、信任度和疫苗接种意愿,特别是在错误信息、文化误解和难以获得可靠健康信息的背景下。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究采用调查研究设计,通过向选定州的居民发放结构化问卷收集数据。次级数据来源于广播节目档案和公共卫生报告。问卷回答通过简单百分比分析来量化公众在认知、知识和行为方面的趋势,次级数据则通过定性内容分析来评估信息框架、文化相关性和说服策略。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,由于信息设计不佳、文化不匹配和说服内容薄弱,广播信息在减少公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的犹豫态度方面效果有限。这些因素限制了知识获取、信任建立和恐惧减少,从而维持了疫苗的犹豫态度。研究结果表明,在尼日利亚北中部各州,广播作为健康沟通工具在乙型肝炎疫苗接种相关情境下存在显著局限性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本研究指出了广播信息在应对公众犹豫态度方面的局限性,但未提供与其他沟通策略的比较数据。此外,未提及广播信息在不同人口群体中的效果差异,以及社会经济状况或教育水平等因素如何影响疫苗接种意愿。证据还缺乏关于广播信息对疫苗接种行为的长期影响的信息。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本研究建议应仔细评估并重新设计广播信息,以确保其文化相关性、清晰度和具有说服力的内容,从而建立信任并减少恐惧。同时,广播电台和卫生部门应通过扩大覆盖范围至偏远地区、采用多种当地语言以及采用互动访谈节目和证言等吸引人的节目策略,来解决基础设施和受众相关的问题,以提高公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的接受度和接种率。

abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎仍然是尼日利亚的主要公共卫生挑战,低疫苗接种接种率因广泛存在的公众犹豫态度而加剧,这种犹豫态度受到错误信息、文化误解以及难以获得可靠健康信息的影响,尤其是在北中部各州。应对这一挑战需要有效的健康沟通策略,以提高公众意识、信任度和疫苗接种意愿。本研究探讨了广播信息在减少公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种犹豫态度方面的有效性,依据计划行为理论(Theory of Planned Behavior),该理论因其强调态度、主观规范和感知行为控制如何影响意图和健康相关决策而被采用。研究采用调查研究设计,通过结构化问卷收集了选定州居民的数据,并辅以从广播节目档案和公共卫生报告中获取的次级数据。问卷回答通过简单百分比分析来量化公众在认知、知识和行为方面的趋势,次级数据则通过定性内容分析来评估信息框架、文化相关性和说服策略。研究结果表明,广播信息的有效性受到信息设计不当、文化不匹配和说服内容薄弱等因素的严重影响,这些因素限制了知识获取、信任建立和恐惧减少,从而维持了疫苗的犹豫态度。此外,广播作为健康沟通工具的潜力受到基础设施限制、受众多样性、语言障碍、不足的节目策略以及缺乏社区参与的制约,这些因素降低了信息的传播范围、相关性和对疫苗接种决策的影响。研究建议应仔细评估并重新设计广播信息,以确保其文化相关性、清晰度和具有说服力的内容,从而建立信任并减少恐惧。同时,广播电台和卫生部门应通过扩大覆盖范围至偏远地区、采用多种当地语言以及采用互动访谈节目和证言等吸引人的节目策略,来解决基础设施和受众相关的问题,以提高公众对乙型肝炎疫苗接种的接受度和接种率。

title: Genotypic variability and the mutational landscape of the hepatitis B virus among HIV‐infected patients living in the regions of Western Siberia (Russia)
abstract: Abstract Background. Hepatitis B is a major public health problem due to its prevalence, complications, and genetic variability, which requires detailed molecular characterization for effective treatment. HIV‐HBV co‐infection exacerbates the course of hepatitis B, increases the risk of liver damage and death, and also reduces the effectiveness of antiviral therapy. The genetic diversity of the hepatitis B virus in HIV‐positive individuals has not been sufficiently studied, so such research is extremely important for developing more effective control and treatment strategies. Materials and methods. The study analyzed 708 blood serum samples were collected from patients with confirmed HIV infection. For primary screening for HBV DNA, a commercial "AmpliSens HBV-FL" kit was used. For the selected positive samples, next-generation sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform was used to obtain full-genomic HBV nucleotide sequences, which were serotyped, genotyped, and analyzed for the presence of clinically significant mutations Objective. To identify and characterize the variants of hepatitis B in HIV‐infected patients from three geographically close regions of Western Siberia (Novosibirsk Region, Tomsk Region, and the Altai Republic). The incidence of HBV genetic material in the study group was 8.5% (95% CI = 6.6–10.8). The work analyzed 60 full-genomic sequences of the identified HBV variants. All studied HBV variants were assigned to genotype D, and the distribution of HBV subgenotypes in the regions was different and consistent with previously obtained data. The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants. The results highlight the importance of continuous molecular monitoring for the development of diagnostic strategies, improving the effectiveness of vaccination, and clinical management of HBV patients, especially among people living with HIV.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genotypic variability and mutational landscape of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) among HIV-infected patients in three regions of Western Siberia. The research aimed to characterize HBV variants in this population, as HBV genetic diversity is critical for effective treatment and management. A total of 708 blood serum samples were analyzed, with 8.5% testing positive for HBV. Of these, 60 full-genomic sequences were obtained and classified as genotype D. Mutations in the S gene, BCP, PreCore, Core, and X genes were detected in all sequences, with high prevalence in the Core and X genes. The study emphasizes the need for continuous molecular monitoring to improve diagnostic strategies and clinical care for HBV patients, especially those co-infected with HIV. While the findings are significant for understanding HBV dynamics in this specific population, the study's moderate confidence is due to its limited geographic scope and focus on a particular demographic group.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别和表征来自俄罗斯西西伯利亚地区三个地理相邻区域(新西伯利亚地区、托姆斯克地区和阿尔泰共和国)的HIV感染患者中的乙型肝炎病毒变异体。由于乙型肝炎病毒(乙型肝炎病毒)的患病率、并发症和遗传变异,乙型肝炎是主要的公共卫生问题,需要详细的分子特征分析以实现有效的治疗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了708份来自确诊HIV感染患者的血液清样本。在研究组中,HBV遗传物质的发病率为8.5%(95% CI = 6.6–10.8)。本研究分析了60个已鉴定HBV变异体的全基因组序列。
elements_zh.methods: 为了初步筛查HBV DNA,使用了商业化的"AmpliSens HBV-FL"试剂盒。对于筛选出的阳性样本,采用Illumina MiSeq平台的下一代测序技术获得完整的HBV基因组核苷酸序列,并进行血清型、基因型鉴定以及临床显著突变(突变)的分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(S基因)中,突变的整体检出率为55.0%,BCP 突变为28.3%,PreCore 突变为66.7%,在60个分析的基因组全基因组序列中,Core和X基因中的突变均被检测到。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果强调了持续分子监测在诊断策略开发、提高疫苗接种效果以及HBV患者的临床管理中的重要性,尤其是在HIV感染者中。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为HBV患者的诊断策略、疫苗接种项目和临床管理方法的开发提供信息,特别是对于与HIV共感染的患者。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究的地理范围有限且专注于特定人群,本研究的置信度中等,但结果得到了对全基因组序列进行详细分子分析的支持。

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒在俄罗斯西西伯利亚地区HIV感染患者中的基因型变异及突变图谱
source_body_en: Abstract Background. Hepatitis B is a major public health problem due to its prevalence, complications, and genetic variability, which requires detailed molecular characterization for effective treatment. HIV‐HBV co‐infection exacerbates the course of hepatitis B, increases the risk of liver damage and death, and also reduces the effectiveness of antiviral therapy. The genetic diversity of the hepatitis B virus in HIV‐positive individuals has not been sufficiently studied, so such research is extremely important for developing more effective control and treatment strategies. Materials and methods. The study analyzed 708 blood serum samples were collected from patients with confirmed HIV infection. For primary screening for HBV DNA, a commercial "AmpliSens HBV-FL" kit was used. For the selected positive samples, next-generation sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform was used to obtain full-genomic HBV nucleotide sequences, which were serotyped, genotyped, and analyzed for the presence of clinically significant mutations Objective. To identify and characterize the variants of hepatitis B in HIV‐infected patients from three geographically close regions of Western Siberia (Novosibirsk Region, Tomsk Region, and the Altai Republic). The incidence of HBV genetic material in the study group was 8.5% (95% CI = 6.6–10.8). The work analyzed 60 full-genomic sequences of the identified HBV variants. All studied HBV variants were assigned to genotype D, and the distribution of HBV subgenotypes in the regions was different and consistent with previously obtained data. The overall detection rate of mutations in the hepatitis B virus surface antigen (S gene) was 55.0%, BCP mutations – 28.3%, PreCore mutations – 66.7%, mutations in the Core and X genes were detected in each of the 60 analyzed genome-wide sequences of HBV variants. The results highlight the importance of continuous molecular monitoring for the development of diagnostic strategies, improving the effectiveness of vaccination, and clinical management of HBV patients, especially among people living with HIV.

title: Knowledge, Attitude and Practice Regarding Hepatitis-B Virus Infection among Slum Population of Dhaka City, Bangladesh
abstract: Background: The Hepatitis B virus(HBV) infection is an important cause of mortality and morbidity in developing countries. Prevalence rate of HBV infection differs from country to country. In Bangladesh, there have been few small-scale studies on seroprevalence of HBV infection in selective class of people. But no population-based data is available to assess disease burden and draw large-scale intervention measure in slum area of Dhaka City. Objective: To assess knowledge, attitudes, and Practice regarding hepatitis B virus infection in a low-literacy urban population. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted to estimate to the knowledge, attitude and practices of slum people regarding viral hepatitis. The study was carried out among the 2000 adult slum population of Dhaka city, Bangladesh during the year July 2006 to June 2007. There are 4966 slum clusters in Dhaka city. Subjects’ selection from each cluster was by simple random sampling method. Trained interviewers were recruited for data collection with well-designed and structured validated questionnaires. After the collection of data, 3-5 ml of blood from each individual was drawn for HbsAg testing. The ELISA method confirmed HbsAg in cases where it was positive. Results: The majority of participants (82.57%) had general knowledge about hepatitis, but specific understanding was limited. Out of 2000 subjects 828 (41%) were male and 1172 (59%) were female. Mean (±SD) age was 31.91(±11.34) yrs. Among them 1062 (31.10%) were illiterate, 522 (26.10%) had primary level education; 318(15.9%), 54(2.7%) and 44(2.2%) were SSC, HSC and graduates respectively. They came from diverse occupations: house wife- 602 (30%), day laborer- 340 (17%) and industryworker-190(10%). Mean (±SD) house hold population size was 4.91(±2.13). Regarding knowledge of jaundice, a total of 1651(82.57%) had heard the name of jaundice and the rest of the population had not heard the name. Regarding the source of information about jaundice, 1529(76.45%) people had gained knowledge from other public and 262(13.12%) from electronic and print media. Only 16 (0.77%) had gathered knowledge from doctors and health workers. About the symptoms of jaundice, 1034(51.72%) said yellow coloration of urine, 276(13.78%) said yellow coloration of eye, 537(26.86%) said anorexia and 146(7.31%) had no knowledge. Among the study population 1081(54.05%) subjects had past history of jaundice. Regarding the knowledge about infective cause of jaundice, 1859(92.94%) had no knowledge. Only 7.06% knew HBV could be caused by an infectious agent, and 53.99% were unaware of transmission modes. Vaccination rates were low, with only 2.33% having received the HBV vaccine. Risk factors included receiving injections from unqualified providers (16.96%) and using disposable syringes (20.91%). Tobacco use (28.48%) and smoking (18.96%) were common addictions. Conclusion: Knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in Dhaka City’s urban slums. Despite this, residents show interest in learning more and getting tested, though they prefer traditional healers over modern healthcare due to economic and educational constraints. Risk factors for HBV include overcrowding, young age, male sex, barbershop shaving, and low vaccination rates. These findings underscore the need for improved education, healthcare access, and targeted interventions in these communities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B virus infection in a low-literacy urban population. The background highlights that HBV infection is a significant cause of mortality and morbidity in developing countries, with prevalence rates varying by country.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted among 2000 adult slum residents in Dhaka City, Bangladesh, from July 2006 to June 2007. The population was selected through simple random sampling from 4966 slum clusters in the city.
analysis.methods: Trained interviewers collected data using validated questionnaires. Blood samples were taken from each participant for HbsAg testing, and the ELISA method confirmed positive cases.
analysis.main_results: 82.57% of participants had general knowledge about hepatitis, but specific understanding was limited. Only 7.06% knew HBV could be caused by an infectious agent, and 53.99% were unaware of transmission modes. Additionally, 2.33% had received the HBV vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in Dhaka City’s urban slums, despite residents showing interest in learning more and getting tested.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for improved education and healthcare access in these communities to address the poor knowledge and low vaccination rates related to HBV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and the potential for recall bias. The evidence is moderate as it provides descriptive data on knowledge and risk factors but lacks longitudinal or causal analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection among the slum population of Dhaka City, Bangladesh. It found that while 82.57% of participants had general knowledge about hepatitis, specific understanding of HBV causes and transmission modes was limited. Only 2.33% had received the HBV vaccine, and risk factors included low literacy, economic constraints, and limited access to healthcare. The authors concluded that knowledge about viral hepatitis is poor in these communities, emphasizing the need for improved education and healthcare access. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是发展中国家肝硬化和发病率的重要原因。HBV感染的患病率因国家而异。在孟加拉国,针对特定人群的HBV感染研究较少,但目前尚无基于人口的数据来评估贫民区的疾病负担并制定大规模干预措施。目的:评估低文化水平城市人群中对乙型肝炎病毒感染的知识、态度和实践。方法:本横断面研究旨在估计贫民区居民对病毒性肝炎的知识、态度和实践。研究在2006年7月至2007年6月期间,针对孟加拉国达卡市的2000名成年贫民区居民进行。达卡市共有4966个贫民区聚类,每个聚类通过简单随机抽样方法选择受试者。招募了经过培训的访谈员,使用经过良好设计和结构验证的问卷进行数据收集。在收集数据后,从每位受试者身上抽取3-5毫升血液进行HBsAg检测。ELISA方法确认了HBsAg阳性病例。结果:大多数参与者(82.57%)对肝炎有一般性了解,但具体理解有限。在2000名受试者中,828名(41%)为男性,1172名(59%)为女性。平均(±SD)年龄为31.91(±11.34)岁。其中1062名(31.10%)为文盲,522名(26.10%)接受过小学教育;318名(15.9%)、54名(2.7%)和44名(2.2%)分别接受过中等教育、高中教育和大学教育。他们的职业多样:家庭主妇602名(30%),日工340名(17%),工业工人190名(10%)。平均(±SD)家庭人口规模为4.91(±2.13)。关于黄疸的知识,共有1651名(82.57%)参与者听说过黄疸这个名字,其余的人则没有。关于黄疸信息的来源,1529名(76.45%)参与者通过其他公共渠道获得知识,262名(13.12%)通过电子和印刷媒体获得知识。仅有16名(0.77%)参与者从医生和卫生工作者处获得知识。关于黄疸的症状,1034名(51.72%)参与者提到尿液变黄,276名(13.78%)提到眼睛变黄,537名(26.86%)提到食欲不振,146名(7.31%)则没有相关知识。在研究人群中,1081名(54.05%)有黄疸的既往病史。关于黄疸的感染原因,1859名(92.94%)参与者没有相关知识。仅有7.06%的参与者知道HBV是由传染性病原体引起的,而53.99%的参与者不了解传播方式。疫苗接种率较低,仅有2.33%的参与者接种过HBV疫苗。风险因素包括从非合格提供者处接受注射(16.96%)和使用一次性针头(20.91%)。烟草使用(28.48%)和吸烟(18.96%)是常见的成瘾行为。结论:达卡市城市贫民区对病毒性肝炎的知识较为匮乏。尽管如此,居民表现出学习更多知识和接受检测的兴趣,但由于经济和教育限制,他们更倾向于选择传统治疗者而非现代医疗。HBV的风险因素包括拥挤、年轻年龄、男性性别、理发店刮脸以及疫苗接种率低。这些发现强调了在这些社区中改善教育、医疗可及性和针对性干预的必要性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估低文化水平城市人群中对乙型肝炎病毒感染的知识、态度和实践。背景指出,HBV感染是发展中国家肝硬化和发病率的重要原因,其患病率因国家而异。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本横断面研究在孟加拉国达卡市的2000名成年贫民区居民中进行,时间为2006年7月至2007年6月。该人群通过简单随机抽样方法从达卡市的4966个贫民区聚类中选取。
analysis_zh.methods: 经过培训的访谈员使用经过验证的问卷收集数据。从每位参与者身上抽取血液样本进行HBsAg检测,并通过ELISA方法确认阳性病例。
analysis_zh.main_results: 82.57%的参与者对肝炎有一般性了解,但具体理解有限。仅有7.06%的参与者知道HBV是由传染性病原体引起的,而53.99%的参与者不了解传播方式。此外,2.33%的参与者接种过HBV疫苗。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,达卡市城市贫民区对病毒性肝炎的知识较为匮乏,尽管居民表现出学习更多知识和接受检测的兴趣。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了在这些社区中改善教育和医疗可及性的必要性,以应对与HBV感染相关的知识匮乏和疫苗接种率低的问题。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于依赖于自我报告数据,可能存在回忆偏差。证据强度中等,因为它提供了关于知识和风险因素的描述性数据,但缺乏纵向或因果分析。

title: Awareness and Preventive Practices of Hepatitis B Virus Infection Among Pregnant Women in Bangladesh
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major global health challenge, particularly concerning for pregnant women due to the risk of vertical transmission. Although vaccines and antiviral therapies are available, public awareness and preventive practices in Bangladesh remain insufficient. Objective: This study aimed to examine the relationship between awareness and preventive practices of HBV infection among pregnant women in Bangladesh. Methods: A descriptive correlational study design was conducted at the 250-Bedded General Hospital in Kushtia. A total of 112 pregnant women were selected through a convenience sampling technique. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using structured questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Results: The study found that 80.4% of participants demonstrated limited awareness regarding disease transmission, symptoms, screening procedures, and vaccination. Furthermore, 75% of participants reported insufficient engagement in preventive practices. These findings highlight a substantial deficiency in both awareness and implementation of preventive behaviors. Socio-demographic variables, including educational level, occupation, monthly family income, and place of residence, were significantly associated with awareness and preventive practices. Conclusion: Awareness of HBV infection among pregnant women was inadequate, and their preventive practices were also limited. Therefore, comprehensive health education programs are recommended to be implemented during antenatal visits to increase awareness and improve preventive behaviors among pregnant women in Bangladesh.
journal: International Journal of Maternal Perinatal and Neonatal Care

abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是全球主要的公共卫生挑战,尤其对孕妇而言,由于存在垂直传播的风险。尽管疫苗和抗病毒药物疗法已可用,但孟加拉国公众对HBV感染的认知和预防措施仍显不足。目的:本研究旨在探讨孟加拉国孕妇对HBV感染的认知与预防措施之间的关系。方法:在Kushtia的250床综合医院进行了一项描述性相关性研究,通过便利抽样方法选取了112名孕妇。数据通过面对面访谈和结构化问卷收集,并使用描述性和推断性统计方法进行分析。结果:研究发现,80.4%的参与者对疾病传播、症状、筛查程序和疫苗接种的认知有限。此外,75%的参与者报告称在预防措施上的参与不足。这些发现突显了孟加拉国孕妇在认知和预防行为实施方面存在显著的不足。社会人口学变量,包括教育水平、职业、月家庭收入和居住地,与认知和预防措施显著相关。结论:孟加拉国孕妇对HBV感染的认知不足,其预防措施也有限。因此,建议在产前检查期间实施全面的健康教育项目,以提高孕妇对HBV感染的认知并改善其预防行为。

title: Assessment of Knowledge and Awareness Regarding Transmission and Risk Factors of HBV, HCV, and HIV among Health Sciences Students in Universities of Taiz, Yemen
abstract: Abstract Background Health sciences students are at risk of occupational exposure to blood-borne pathogens, including hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). The aim of this study was to evaluate the knowledge, awareness, attitudes, preventive practices and occupational exposure of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen. Methods A descriptive analytical cross sectional study was carried on 505 health sciences students in five universities in Taiz, Yemen from September 2025 to July 2026. The sampling method for the participants was stratified sampling, based on university, discipline and academic year. A self-administered, structured questionnaire was used to collect data, which included knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, vaccination status for HBV, and occupational exposure. Data analysis was done using descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi square tests in SPSS statistics. Results Mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, 50.7% of students had good knowledge. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, awareness, attitudes, preventive practices and occupational exposure of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 505 health sciences students across five universities in Taiz, Yemen from September 2025 to July 2026.
analysis.methods: Stratified sampling was used to select participants based on university, discipline, and academic year. Data were collected using a self-administered, structured questionnaire that assessed knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, vaccination status for HBV, and occupational exposure.
analysis.main_results: The mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, with 50.7% of students having good knowledge. Students at the clinical stage had higher good knowledge rates compared to pre-clinical students (57.0% vs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight a significant knowledge gap among health sciences students, particularly in pre-clinical stages, and suggest the need for targeted educational interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform the development of educational programs to improve HBV awareness and preventive practices among health sciences students, which is critical for reducing occupational transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and self-reported data, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the knowledge and awareness of health sciences students in Taiz, Yemen, regarding hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A descriptive analytical cross-sectional study was conducted on 505 students across five universities from September 2025 to July 2026, using stratified sampling and a self-administered questionnaire. The mean knowledge score was 6.14 ± 1.98 out of 10, with 50.7% of students demonstrating good knowledge. Clinical-stage students had higher good knowledge rates than pre-clinical students (57.0% vs. 34.0%, p < 0.05). The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting a significant knowledge gap, particularly among pre-clinical students, and emphasized the need for targeted educational interventions. The study's results can inform the development of educational programs to improve HBV awareness and preventive practices among health sciences students, which is essential for reducing occupational transmission risks. However, the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Post-vaccination immunity to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel: predictive modeling, key predictors, and risk management
abstract: Objective : to analyze the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel to determine prognostic criteria and risk management. Materials and methods : the results of serological screening of 1,380 employees of a multidisciplinary medical center for anti-HBsAg, HBsAg in 2024-2025 and their vaccination history data were analyzed. Laboratory tests were performed on the basis of the laboratory of the European Medical Center “UMMC-Health” by enzyme immunoassay using a set of reagents “Vecto HBsAg-antibodies”, JSC “Vector-Best”. The protective concentration of specific antibodies in the blood serum was considered to be 10 mIU/ml or more. Statistical processing was performed in Microsoft Office Excel 2016 and SPSS Statistics (v. Results: in 81.8% of the employees, the concentration of anti-HBsAg was more than 10 mIU/ml. When constructing a binary logistic regression model (p<0,001), it was found that increasing the age of employees by 1 year lowered the chances of a positive result by 1,052 times. An increase in the period since the last injection of the vaccine for each year reduced the chances of a positive result by 1,055 times. Administration of each additional dose of the vaccine increased the chances of a positive result by 2,036 times. The sensitivity of the model was 73.9%, and the specificity was 73.7%. The overall diagnostic significance of the model is 73.8%. Conclusion : the results of the study indicate the need for further study of the feasibility of booster immunization of medical workers, taking into account a comprehensive assessment of humoral and cellular immunity, in order to effectively manage biological risks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel to determine prognostic criteria and risk management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed serological screening results of 1,380 employees from a multidisciplinary medical center for anti-HBsAg and HBsAg in 2024-2025, along with their vaccination history data.
analysis.methods: Laboratory tests were conducted using enzyme immunoassay with the reagent set “Vecto HBsAg-antibodies” from JSC “Vector-Best”. A binary logistic regression model was constructed to identify predictors of positive immune response.
analysis.main_results: In 81.8% of the employees, the concentration of anti-HBsAg was more than 10 mIU/ml. Increasing age by 1 year lowered the chances of a positive result by 1,052 times. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating the need for further study on the feasibility of booster immunization for medical workers, considering a comprehensive assessment of humoral and cellular immunity to effectively manage biological risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted booster immunization strategies for medical personnel to enhance post-vaccination immunity and reduce the risk of hepatitis B virus exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on serological data and a binary logistic regression model, which may not fully capture the complexity of immune responses. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the post-vaccination immune response to hepatitis B virus in medical personnel, focusing on predictive modeling and key predictors. It analyzed serological screening data from 1,380 employees over 2024-2025, using enzyme immunoassay to measure anti-HBsAg levels. The results showed that 81.8% of employees had antibody concentrations above 10 mIU/ml, with age, time since last vaccination, and number of doses significantly affecting the likelihood of a positive result. The model demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity, suggesting its potential utility in risk management. The authors concluded that further research on booster immunization, incorporating both humoral and cellular immunity assessments, is necessary to improve hepatitis B virus risk management strategies in medical settings.
