abstract_zh: 目的:分析疫苗接种后医疗人员对乙型肝炎病毒的免疫力,以确定预后标准和风险管理。方法:分析了2024-2025年某多学科医疗中心1,380名员工的血清学筛查结果,包括抗-HBsAg、HBsAg以及他们的疫苗接种历史数据。实验室检测基于欧洲医疗中心“UMMC-Health”实验室,使用JSC“媒介-Best”提供的试剂盒“Vecto HBsAg-antibodies”进行酶免疫分析。认为血清中特定抗体的保护浓度为10 mIU/ml或以上。统计处理使用Microsoft Office Excel 2016和SPSS Statistics(v. 结果:81.8%的员工抗-HBsAg浓度超过10 mIU/ml。构建二元逻辑回归模型(p<0,001)时发现,员工年龄每增加1岁,阳性结果的可能性降低1,052倍。自上次接种疫苗以来的时间每增加1年,阳性结果的可能性降低1,055倍。每增加一次疫苗接种,阳性结果的可能性增加2,036倍。模型的敏感度为73.9%,特异度为73.7%,整体诊断意义为73.8%。结论:研究结果表明,需要进一步研究医疗人员加强免疫接种的可行性,综合评估体液和细胞免疫,以有效管理生物风险。

title: Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 levels in treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B: associations with EASL-based clinical phenotypes, histological inflammatory activity, and non-invasive fibrosis indices
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major global health issue, as ongoing viral replication can drive hepatic inflammation and immune dysregulation, increasing the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. CXCL-10, a proinflammatory chemokine, and CTLA-4, an inhibitory immune checkpoint, may each capture a different facet of the immune response in CHB. This study evaluated serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 in CHB patients and their associations with HBV DNA, laboratory findings, and non-invasive fibrosis markers. In total, 86 individuals were enrolled: 21 healthy controls and 65 treatment-naive CHB patients. CHB patients were categorized by HBV DNA level into ≤ 105 IU/mL ( n = 33) and > 105 IU/mL ( n = 32). Patients were also classified into EASL (European Association for the Study of the Liver)-based clinical phenotypes using HBeAg status, HBV DNA, and ALT. Liver biopsy data (Ishak fibrosis stage and modified Ishak HAI score) were available for 43 patients (66.2%). FIB-4 was calculated for all participants. Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were measured by ELISA, and laboratory-based inflammatory and fibrosis-related indices were calculated. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were used to assess associations; ROC analyses were descriptive and exploratory. Serum levels of CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 differed significantly among study groups and were highest in patients with elevated viral loads (both p < 0.001). Viral load correlated strongly with CXCL-10 ( r = 0.786) and CTLA-4 ( r = 0.559), and CXCL-10 correlated strongly with CTLA-4 ( r = 0.690; all p < 0.001). Both CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 correlated more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score ( r = 0.519 and r = 0.509, respectively; p < 0.001) than with fibrosis stage. CXCL-10 levels were elevated in Phase 2 (HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis) compared to Phase 3 ( p < 0.001) and Phase 4 ( p = 0.005). The descriptive ROC performance was moderate (AUC 0.78 for CXCL-10; 0.76 for CTLA-4, sensitivity 47%); in an exploratory analysis, CXCL-10 differentiated high (HAI ≥ 7) from low histological activity (AUC 0.77). Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were associated with HBV DNA, biochemical liver injury, and histological inflammatory activity in treatment-naive CHB, correlating more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score than with fibrosis stage. These findings suggest a role for CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 as markers of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activity in CHB, warranting confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.

title_zh: 治疗初发者慢性乙型肝炎: 与基于EASL的临床表型、组织学炎症活动度及非侵入性纤维化指标相关的血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平
source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major global health issue, as ongoing viral replication can drive hepatic inflammation and immune dysregulation, increasing the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. CXCL-10, a proinflammatory chemokine, and CTLA-4, an inhibitory immune checkpoint, may each capture a different facet of the immune response in CHB. This study evaluated serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 in CHB patients and their associations with HBV DNA, laboratory findings, and non-invasive fibrosis markers. In total, 86 individuals were enrolled: 21 healthy controls and 65 treatment-naive CHB patients. CHB patients were categorized by HBV DNA level into ≤ 105 IU/mL ( n = 33) and > 105 IU/mL ( n = 32). Patients were also classified into EASL (European Association for the Study of the Liver)-based clinical phenotypes using HBeAg status, HBV DNA, and ALT. Liver biopsy data (Ishak fibrosis stage and modified Ishak HAI score) were available for 43 patients (66.2%). FIB-4 was calculated for all participants. Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were measured by ELISA, and laboratory-based inflammatory and fibrosis-related indices were calculated. Group comparisons and correlation analyses were used to assess associations; ROC analyses were descriptive and exploratory. Serum levels of CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 differed significantly among study groups and were highest in patients with elevated viral loads (both p < 0.001). Viral load correlated strongly with CXCL-10 ( r = 0.786) and CTLA-4 ( r = 0.559), and CXCL-10 correlated strongly with CTLA-4 ( r = 0.690; all p < 0.001). Both CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 correlated more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score ( r = 0.519 and r = 0.509, respectively; p < 0.001) than with fibrosis stage. CXCL-10 levels were elevated in Phase 2 (HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis) compared to Phase 3 ( p < 0.001) and Phase 4 ( p = 0.005). The descriptive ROC performance was moderate (AUC 0.78 for CXCL-10; 0.76 for CTLA-4, sensitivity 47%); in an exploratory analysis, CXCL-10 differentiated high (HAI ≥ 7) from low histological activity (AUC 0.77). Serum CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 were associated with HBV DNA, biochemical liver injury, and histological inflammatory activity in treatment-naive CHB, correlating more strongly with the modified Ishak HAI score than with fibrosis stage. These findings suggest a role for CXCL-10 and CTLA-4 as markers of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activity in CHB, warranting confirmation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.
abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)是全球主要的健康问题,因为持续的病毒复制可驱动肝炎和免疫失调,增加肝硬化和肝细胞癌的风险。CXCL-10是一种促炎性趋化因子,而CTLA-4是一种抑制性免疫检查点,它们可能分别反映慢性乙型肝炎中不同的方面。本研究评估了慢性乙型肝炎患者血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平及其与HBV DNA、实验室检查结果和非侵入性纤维化标志物之间的关联。共纳入86名受试者:21名健康对照者和65名治疗初发的慢性乙型肝炎患者。根据HBV DNA水平,将慢性乙型肝炎患者分为≤105 IU/mL(n=33)和>105 IU/mL(n=32)两组。患者还根据HBeAg状态、HBV DNA和ALT水平被分为基于EASL(欧洲肝脏研究协会)的临床表型。43名患者(66.2%)提供了肝脏活检数据(Ishak纤维化分期和改良Ishak HAI评分)。对所有参与者计算了FIB-4。通过ELISA检测血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平,并计算了基于实验室的炎症和纤维化相关指标。通过组间比较和相关性分析评估了这些关联;ROC分析为描述性和探索性分析。血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平在不同研究组间存在显著差异,且在病毒载量升高的患者中最高(两者p<0.001)。病毒载量与CXCL-10(r=0.786)和CTLA-4(r=0.559)呈强相关,而CXCL-10与CTLA-4也呈强相关(r=0.690;所有p<0.001)。CXCL-10和CTLA-4与改良Ishak HAI评分的相关性(分别为r=0.519和r=0.509;p<0.001)强于与纤维化分期的相关性。与Phase 3(p=0.005)和Phase 4相比,Phase 2(HBeAg阳性慢性肝炎)患者的CXCL-10水平升高(p<0.001)。描述性ROC分析的性能中等(CXCL-10的AUC为0.78;CTLA-4的AUC为0.76,灵敏度为47%);在探索性分析中,CXCL-10可区分高(HAI≥7)与低组织学活动(AUC为0.77)。血清CXCL-10和CTLA-4水平与治疗初发的慢性乙型肝炎患者的HBV DNA、生化肝损伤及组织学炎症活动度相关,且与改良Ishak HAI评分的相关性强于与纤维化分期的相关性。这些发现表明,CXCL-10和CTLA-4可能作为慢性乙型肝炎中炎症和免疫调节活动的标志物,需要在更大规模、纵向研究中进行验证。

title: SEROLOGICAL CLEARANCE OF HBSAG IN CHRONIC HEPATITIS B: EXPERIENCE IN A UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL
abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major public health problem due to its high morbidity and mortality associated with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Functional cure, characterized by serological clearance of the HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), is the main therapeutic goal, since sterilizing viral eradication is not yet feasible. HBsAg clearance rates vary widely in the literature, and understanding the factors associated with this event is crucial for optimizing patient management. Objective: To investigate the HBsAg clearance rate and identify the demographic, clinical, and virological factors associated with this event in a cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection followed up at a reference center in Northeast Brazil. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted through a review of the medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection treated at a Hepatology Service in Northeast Brazil between January 2015 and October 2025. Clinical, demographic and laboratory variables were analyzed. Statistical analysis used tests such as Mann-Whitney for quantitative variables and Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, in addition to the construction of Kaplan-Meier curves with the Log-Rank test to evaluate HBsAg clearance. The significance level was set at P<0.05. Results: Of the 600 medical records screened, 299 patients were included in the analysis, 63.2% of whom were women, with a median age of 45 years. During a mean follow-up period of 5.14 years, totaling 1,538 person-years, 12 patients (4%) achieved serological clearance of HBsAg, resulting in an annual rate of 0.78%. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations between HBsAg clearance and advanced age (P=0.008) and lower HBV-DNA levels (P=0.0156). Conclusion: The annual rate of HBsAg serological clearance in this cohort was 0.78%. Advanced age and low viral load levels were significantly associated with functional cure. These findings enrich the knowledge about the natural history of chronic hepatitis B in the region and reaffirm the importance of viral suppression in disease control.

title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎病毒血清学清除:巴西东北部大学医院的经验
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection represents a major public health problem due to its high morbidity and mortality associated with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Functional cure, characterized by serological clearance of the HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), is the main therapeutic goal, since sterilizing viral eradication is not yet feasible. HBsAg clearance rates vary widely in the literature, and understanding the factors associated with this event is crucial for optimizing patient management. Objective: To investigate the HBsAg clearance rate and identify the demographic, clinical, and virological factors associated with this event in a cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection followed up at a reference center in Northeast Brazil. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted through a review of the medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection treated at a Hepatology Service in Northeast Brazil between January 2015 and October 2025. Clinical, demographic and laboratory variables were analyzed. Statistical analysis used tests such as Mann-Whitney for quantitative variables and Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, in addition to the construction of Kaplan-Meier curves with the Log-Rank test to evaluate HBsAg clearance. The significance level was set at P<0.05. Results: Of the 600 medical records screened, 299 patients were included in the analysis, 63.2% of whom were women, with a median age of 45 years. During a mean follow-up period of 5.14 years, totaling 1,538 person-years, 12 patients (4%) achieved serological clearance of HBsAg, resulting in an annual rate of 0.78%. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations between HBsAg clearance and advanced age (P=0.008) and lower HBV-DNA levels (P=0.0156). Conclusion: The annual rate of HBsAg serological clearance in this cohort was 0.78%. Advanced age and low viral load levels were significantly associated with functional cure. These findings enrich the knowledge about the natural history of chronic hepatitis B in the region and reaffirm the importance of viral suppression in disease control.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染由于其高发病率以及与肝硬化和肝细胞癌相关的特性,构成了重大的公共卫生问题。功能性治愈,以HBV表面抗原(HBsAg)的血清学清除为特征,是主要的治疗目标,因为目前尚无法实现病毒的完全清除。HBsAg清除率在文献中存在较大差异,了解与这一事件相关的因素对于优化患者管理至关重要。目的:探讨慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染患者在巴西东北部参考中心随访的队列研究中HBsAg清除率,并识别与该事件相关的流行病学、临床和病毒学因素。方法:通过回顾2015年1月至2025年10月期间在巴西东北部某肝病科治疗的慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染患者的医疗记录,进行了一项回顾性队列研究研究。分析了临床、人口统计学和实验室变量。统计分析采用Mann-Whitney检验用于定量变量,Fisher精确检验用于分类变量,同时构建Kaplan-Meier曲线并使用Log-Rank检验评估HBsAg清除情况。显著性水平设定为P<0.05。结果:在筛选的600份医疗记录中,有299名患者被纳入分析,其中63.2%为女性,中位年龄为45岁。在平均随访期5.14年,总计1,538人年的观察中,12名患者(4%)实现了HBsAg的血清学清除,年清除率为0.78%。统计分析显示,HBsAg清除与年龄较大(P=0.008)和较低的HBV-DNA水平(P=0.0156)存在显著关联。结论:在该队列研究中,HBsAg血清学清除的年发生率为0.78%。年龄较大和病毒载量较低与功能性治愈显著相关。这些发现丰富了该地区慢性乙型肝炎病毒自然史的知识,并重申了病毒抑制在疾病控制中的重要性。

title: Depression and medication adherence among chronic hepatitis B patients receiving resilience-based care versus standard care during antiviral therapy: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care and depressive symptoms and medication adherence among patients with CHB receiving antiviral therapy. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, 200 patients diagnosed with CHB and treated at our hospital's hepatology clinic between July 2022 and June 2025 were included. Based on historical records, 100 patients who voluntarily completed a structured 12-week resilience promotion program in addition to standard care formed the observation group, and 100 patients who received standard care only formed the control group. Primary outcomes at the 6-month follow-up were depressive symptom severity measured by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and medication adherence measured by the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR). Secondary outcomes included resilience (Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale-10, CD-RISC-10), virological response, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization, quality of life (SF-36), adverse events, and healthcare utilization. To account for potential confounding by indication and baseline imbalances, multivariable linear, logistic, and Poisson regression models were used, with adjusted effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals reported. Results At the 6-month follow-up, the observation group had lower depression scores (6.78 ± 3.45 vs. 10.23 ± 4.12), higher MPR (0.92 ± 0.08 vs. 0.78 ± 0.15), and higher resilience scores (32.45 ± 5.67 vs. Virological response (85.0% vs. 70.0%; adjusted OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.48) and ALT normalization (80.0% vs. 65.0%; adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10 to 3.67) were more frequent in the observation group. SF-36 physical and mental component scores were also higher in the observation group. Adverse event incidence was similar between groups. The observation group had fewer unplanned outpatient visits ( P = 0.045), and Poisson regression confirmed fewer outpatient visits in the observation group (adjusted rate ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.93). However, because allocation was non-randomized, these associations may be affected by self-selection and residual confounding. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort study, receiving a resilience-focused program in addition to standard care was associated with lower depressive symptoms, better medication adherence, and more favorable virological and biochemical outcomes in patients with CHB.

title: Near-Full-Length Hepatitis B Virus Genomes Isolated from Cerebrospinal Fluid of People Living with HIV and Cryptococcal Meningitis in Botswana
abstract: Background/Objectives: Increasing evidence suggests that the hepatitis B virus (HBV) can be detected in extrahepatic compartments. Data on the molecular characteristics of HBV in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) remain limited, particularly among people living with HIV (PLWH) and cryptococcal meningitis (CM). This study aimed to characterize HBV genomes from plasma and CSF and compare paired sequences for genetic similarity and potential compartment-specific differences. Methods: Archived plasma and CSF samples from PLWH with CM from Botswana enrolled in AMBITION-CM trial (2018–2021) were sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technology to generate near-full-length HBV genomes. Genotyping and mutational analysis were performed and paired plasma–CSF sequences were compared. Results: Four sequences were generated, including one plasma–CSF pair and two CSF-only sequences. The sequences clustered with genotypes A1 and D3. The single paired plasma–CSF sequences shared 98.8% nucleotide similarity, and clustered together with strong phylogenetic support (SH-aLRT/ultrafast bootstrap = 99.6/100). Variant analysis identified 492 and 545 high-quality variants (Q ≥ 30) in plasma and CSF, respectively. In the single paired sequences, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutation T1858C was detected in plasma but not in the CSF. Mutations were also identified in CSF-derived sequences, including A1762T/G1764A, G1896A, G1899A, associated with increased HCC risk, rtS184L, rtF194L, rtP236T, linked to antiviral resistance and sP127L, sQ129L, sM133L, sS136P, associated with immune escape. Conclusions: Near-full-length HBV genomes were successfully recovered and genetically characterized from the CSF of PLWH with CM. The single plasma–CSF paired sample, showed high genetic similarity and had a compartment-specific mutation. Clinically relevant mutations were observed in the CSF warranting further investigation of HBV in the CSF to confirm these observations in PLWH with CM. These preliminary findings from a limited number of participants provide a basis for larger-scale studies of near-full-length HBV genome characterization in CSF.

Methods: Archived plasma and CSF samples from PLWH with CM from Botswana enrolled in AMBITION-CM trial (2018–2021) were sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technology to generate near-full-length HBV genomes. Genotyping and mutational analysis were performed and paired plasma–CSF sequences were compared. Results: Four sequences were generated, including one plasma–CSF pair and two CSF-only sequences. The sequences clustered with genotypes A1 and D3. The single paired plasma–CSF sequences shared 98.8% nucleotide similarity, and clustered together with strong phylogenetic support (SH-aLRT/ultrafast bootstrap = 99.6/100). Variant analysis identified 492 and 545 high-quality variants (Q ≥ 30) in plasma and CSF, respectively. In the single paired sequences, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)-associated mutation T1858C was detected in plasma but not in the CSF. Mutations were also identified in CSF-derived sequences, including A1762T/G1764A, G1896A, G1899A, associated with increased HCC risk, rtS184L, rtF194L, rtP236T, linked to antiviral resistance and sP127L, sQ129L, sM133L, sS136P, associated with immune escape. Conclusions: Near-full-length HBV genomes were successfully recovered and genetically characterized from the CSF of PLWH with CM. The single plasma–CSF paired sample, showed high genetic similarity and had a compartment-specific mutation. Clinically relevant mutations were observed in the CSF warranting further investigation of HBV in the CSF to confirm these observations in PLWH with CM. These preliminary findings from a limited number of participants provide a basis for larger-scale studies of near-full-length HBV genome characterization in CSF.

title: The core obstacles and immunological mechanisms in the study of functional cure for Chronic Hepatitis B
abstract: Attaining a functional cure constitutes the paramount therapeutic objective in the management of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), as it markedly reduces the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma and the progression to terminal liver disease. Despite this, the current functional cure rate among CHB patients remains below 30%. Major impediments to achieving this outcome include the persistent existence of viral covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), integration of the viral genome into the host’s DNA, immune tolerance resulting from prolonged exposure to elevated viral antigen levels, and host-mediated HBV-specific immune exhaustion and dysfunction at multiple regulatory levels. A thorough elucidation of the molecular pathways underpinning these barriers, alongside their associated immune regulatory networks, is critical for the advancement of novel therapeutic strategies. This review comprehensively integrates recent progress in understanding the virological mechanisms responsible for HBV persistence, host immune responses to HBV infection, and emerging immunotherapeutic interventions. The aim is to establish a theoretical foundation and provide critical perspectives to support the clinical translation of approaches designed to achieve a functional cure for CHB.

It highlights the persistent obstacles such as viral covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), immune tolerance, and host-mediated immune exhaustion. The review integrates recent findings on virological mechanisms, host immune responses, and immunotherapeutic interventions to provide a theoretical foundation for future clinical applications. It emphasizes the need for a deeper understanding of molecular pathways and immune regulatory networks to develop effective therapeutic strategies. The review also outlines the importance of translating these insights into practical approaches for the treatment of CHB.

abstract_zh: 实现功能性治愈是慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)管理中的首要治疗目标,因为它显著降低了肝细胞癌的发病率并减缓进展至终末期肝病的过程。尽管如此,目前CHB患者中实现功能性治愈的比例仍低于30%。实现这一目标的主要障碍包括病毒共价闭合环状DNA(共价闭合环状DNA)的持续存在、病毒基因组整合至宿主基因组中、由于长期暴露于高水平病毒抗原导致的免疫耐受,以及宿主介导的HBV特异性免疫耗竭和在多个调控层面的功能障碍。对这些障碍背后的分子通路及其相关免疫调控网络进行深入阐明,对于开发新的治疗策略至关重要。本综述全面整合了近期关于HBV持续存在的病毒学机制、宿主对HBV感染的免疫应答以及新兴免疫治疗干预措施的研究进展。其目的是建立理论基础并提供关键视角,以支持旨在实现功能性治愈的CHB治疗方案的临床转化。

title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration
abstract: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity. Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.

title: Novel HEP-FIB score combined with machine learning models for non-invasive prediction of significant hepatic fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B patients: a single-center, internally validated study
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Assessment of hepatic fibrosis is important for risk stratification and guiding treatment in CHB. Liver biopsy, the reference standard for fibrosis staging, is invasive, and fraught with potential complications, creating the need for alternative non-invasive tools. Existing non-invasive fibrosis scores demonstrate variable diagnostic accuracy, and the role of lipids in fibrosis prediction remains insufficiently explored. We developed and internally validated HEP-FIB, a parsimonious score based on routinely available laboratory parameters, and evaluated machine learning (ML) models for non-invasive prediction of significant hepatic fibrosis in CHB patients. A retrospective cohort of 382 CHB patients was analyzed. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression followed by multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of fibrosis. A novel HEP-FIB score was developed based on platelet count, liver function parameters, and lipid biomarkers. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, bootstrap internal validation and calibration analysis. The performance of HEP-FIB was compared with established non-invasive indices, including APRI, FIB-4, and GPR. In addition, ten ML algorithms were constructed and evaluated for predictive performance. ML model performance was evaluated using Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), average precision (AP), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV, precision), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), balanced accuracy, false positive rate (FPR), false negative rate (FNR), and Brier score to allow a comprehensive evaluation of discrimination, classification performance, calibration, and overall predictive ability. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed separately for both HEP-FIB score and ML models to assess clinical utility. The HEP-FIB score demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance, achieving an AUC of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.859–0.925).At the optimal cutoff value (≥ 4), the score showed a sensitivity of 78%, specificity of 89%, and overall accuracy of 88%. HEP-FIB outperformed APRI (AUC 0.724), FIB-4 (AUC 0.654), and GPR (AUC 0.773) (all p < 0.001 by DeLong test). Bootstrap validation showed stable performance with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.881. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed fibrosis probabilities, while DCA demonstrated superior net clinical benefit over default strategies. Among ML approaches, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.914 (95% CI: 0.857–0.971), accuracy of 0.88, sensitivity of 0.72, specificity of 0.93, balanced accuracy of 0.83, and MCC of 0.74 in the validation dataset. The model demonstrated favorable calibration, evidenced by the low Brier score (0.095), together with reduced misclassification errors as reflected by low FPR (0.062) and FNR (0.275). elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对382例慢性乙型肝炎患者进行了回顾性队列研究分析。该研究是一项单中心、内部验证的研究。该研究关注慢性乙型肝炎患者。
elements_zh.methods: 最小绝对值收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归随后进行多变量逻辑回归用于识别纤维化的独立预测因子。我们开发并内部验证了基于常规实验室参数的简明评分系统HEP-FIB,并评估了机器学习(ML)模型在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中非侵入性预测显著肝纤维化的应用。
elements_zh.main_results: HEP-FIB评分表现出优异的诊断性能,实现了0.892的AUC(95% CI:0.859–0.925)。在最佳截断值(≥4)时,该评分显示出78%的灵敏度、89%的特异性和88%的总体准确性。HEP-FIB评分优于APRI(AUC 0.724)、FIB-4(AUC 0.654)和GPR(AUC 0.773)(所有p值均小于0.001,通过DeLong检验)。Bootstrap验证显示其性能稳定,校正乐观后的AUC为0.881。校准分析显示预测与观察到的纤维化概率之间有良好的一致性,而DCA显示其在默认策略上的净临床获益更优。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于血小板计数、肝功能参数和脂质生物标志物开发了一种新的HEP-FIB评分系统。集成机器学习模型在预测准确性方面略优于HEP-FIB评分。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HEP-FIB评分在慢性乙型肝炎中显示出强大的诊断性能,用于识别显著肝纤维化,并在该回顾性、单中心队列研究研究中经过内部自举验证后优于传统的非侵入性纤维化评分。机器学习模型在诊断性能上仅显示出轻微的优势。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在该评分被推荐用于常规临床应用之前,需要在独立且多样化的慢性乙型肝炎人群中进行外部验证。所提供的证据未报告研究结果的普遍适用性。

abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)仍然是全球主要的健康负担。评估肝纤维化对于风险分层和指导治疗(抗病毒药物)治疗至关重要。肝活检作为纤维化分期的参考标准,具有侵入性且可能伴随潜在并发症,因此需要替代的非侵入性工具。现有的非侵入性纤维化评分系统在诊断准确性方面表现不一,且脂质在纤维化预测中的作用尚未被充分探索。我们开发并内部验证了一种基于常规实验室参数的简明评分系统HEP-FIB,并评估了机器学习(ML)模型在慢性乙型肝炎患者中非侵入性预测显著肝纤维化的性能。对382例慢性乙型肝炎患者的回顾性队列研究进行了分析。采用最小绝对值收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归后进行多变量逻辑回归,以确定纤维化的独立预测因子。基于血小板计数、肝功能参数和脂质生物标志物,开发了一种新的HEP-FIB评分系统。使用受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析、自举内部验证和校准分析来评估诊断性能。将HEP-FIB的性能与已有的非侵入性指标进行比较,包括APRI、FIB-4和GPR。此外,构建并评估了十种机器学习算法的预测性能。通过受试者工作特征曲线下的面积(AUC)、平均精度(AP)、准确率、灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值(PPV,精确度)、阴性预测值(NPV)、F1分数、马修斯相关系数(MCC)、平衡准确率、假阳性率(FPR)和假阴性率(FNR)以及布里尔分数(Brier score)来全面评估模型的区分能力、分类性能、校准和整体预测能力。分别对HEP-FIB评分系统和机器学习模型进行决策曲线分析(DCA),以评估其临床实用性。HEP-FIB评分系统表现出优异的诊断性能,其AUC为0.892(95% CI:0.859–0.925)。在最佳截断值(≥4)时,该评分系统显示出78%的灵敏度、89%的特异度和88%的总体准确率。HEP-FIB在内部自举验证后,在回顾性、单中心队列研究中表现出优于APRI(AUC 0.724)、FIB-4(AUC 0.654)和GPR(AUC 0.773)的性能(所有p值均小于0.001,通过DeLong检验)。自举验证显示其性能稳定,乐观校正后的AUC为0.881。校准分析显示预测的纤维化概率与实际观察结果之间有良好一致性,而DCA显示其相对于默认策略具有更高的净临床获益。在机器学习方法中,XGBoost在验证数据集中表现出最佳的预测性能,其AUC为0.914(95% CI:0.857–0.971),准确率为0.88,灵敏度为0.72,特异度为0.93,平衡准确率为0.83,MCC为0.74。该模型表现出良好的校准性能,这体现在较低的布里尔分数(0.095)以及较低的假阳性率(0.062)和假阴性率(0.275)所反映的误分类错误减少。DCA显示机器学习模型相较于测试所有和测试无策略具有更大的净临床获益。机器学习模型在预测性能方面相较于HEP-FIB评分系统表现出轻微优势。HEP-FIB在慢性乙型肝炎患者中表现出强大的诊断性能,能够识别显著肝纤维化,并在回顾性、单中心队列研究中优于传统非侵入性纤维化评分系统。集成机器学习模型在预测准确性方面略优于HEP-FIB评分系统。然而,在独立且多样化的慢性乙型肝炎人群中进行外部验证后,该评分系统才能被推荐用于常规临床实践。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)仍然是全球主要的健康负担。评估肝纤维化对于风险分层和指导治疗在慢性乙型肝炎中的治疗至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对382例慢性乙型肝炎患者进行了回顾性队列研究分析。该研究是一项单中心、内部验证的研究。该研究关注慢性乙型肝炎患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 最小绝对值收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归随后进行多变量逻辑回归用于识别纤维化的独立预测因子。我们开发并内部验证了基于常规实验室参数的简明评分系统HEP-FIB,并评估了机器学习(ML)模型在慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中非侵入性预测显著肝纤维化的应用。
analysis_zh.main_results: HEP-FIB评分表现出优异的诊断性能,实现了0.892的AUC(95% CI:0.859–0.925)。在最佳截断值(≥4)时,该评分显示出78%的灵敏度、89%的特异性和88%的总体准确性。HEP-FIB评分优于APRI(AUC 0.724)、FIB-4(AUC 0.654)和GPR(AUC 0.773)(所有p值均小于0.001,通过DeLong检验)。Bootstrap验证显示其性能稳定,校正乐观后的AUC为0.881。校准分析显示预测与观察到的纤维化概率之间有良好的一致性,而DCA显示其在默认策略上的净临床获益更优。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于血小板计数、肝功能参数和脂质生物标志物开发了一种新的HEP-FIB评分系统。集成机器学习模型在预测准确性方面略优于HEP-FIB评分。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HEP-FIB评分在慢性乙型肝炎中显示出强大的诊断性能,用于识别显著肝纤维化,并在该回顾性、单中心队列研究研究中经过内部自举验证后优于传统的非侵入性纤维化评分。机器学习模型在诊断性能上仅显示出轻微的优势。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在该评分被推荐用于常规临床应用之前,需要在独立且多样化的慢性乙型肝炎人群中进行外部验证。所提供的证据未报告研究结果的普遍适用性。

title: Expression of key factors in the TGF-β1/Smad2 pathway and their associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background This study investigated the expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and evaluated their associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis. Methods In this prospective single-center cohort, 120 patients with HBV-associated HCC were enrolled between April 2022 and April 2024. TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry in paired tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Associations with clinicopathological characteristics and prognosis were examined using correlation analysis, logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Follow-up lasted 12–36 months. Results TGF-β1 and Smad2 expression was significantly higher in tumor tissue than in paired adjacent non-tumor tissue (both P < 0.001). Higher expression was associated with poorer differentiation and more advanced stage ( P < 0.05). Patients with positive TGF-β1 or Smad2 expression had lower survival rates than those with negative expression. The AUCs for predicting death were 0.769 for TGF-β1, 0.756 for Smad2, and 0.892 for the combined model. Conclusions Elevated tumor expression of TGF-β1 and Smad2 is associated with aggressive clinicopathological features and poorer prognosis in HBV-associated HCC. Combined assessment of the two markers may improve prognostic discrimination compared with either marker alone; multicenter validation is warranted.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 本研究探讨了TGF-β1和Smad2在乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝细胞癌(HCC)中的表达,并评估其与临床病理特征和预后的关系。方法 在这项前瞻性单中心研究中,于2022年4月至2024年4月期间纳入了120例乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌患者。通过免疫组化法检测配对肿瘤组织和相邻非肿瘤组织中TGF-β1和Smad2的表达。采用相关分析、逻辑回归、Kaplan-Meier生存分析和受试者工作特征(ROC)分析评估其与临床病理特征和预后的关系。随访时间为12–36个月。结果 肿瘤组织中TGF-β1和Smad2的表达显著高于配对的相邻非肿瘤组织(两者P < 0.001)。高表达与较差的分化程度和更晚期的分期相关(P < 0.05)。TGF-β1或Smad2表达阳性患者死亡率低于表达阴性者。预测死亡的AUC分别为TGF-β1为0.769,Smad2为0.756,联合模型为0.892。结论 乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌中肿瘤组织TGF-β1和Smad2的高表达与更具侵袭性的临床病理特征和较差的预后相关。与单独使用任一标志物相比,联合评估这两个标志物可能提高预后判别的能力;需要多中心验证。

title: Baseline low-level viremia in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma: prognostic significance, risk stratification, and clinical implications
abstract: Introduction The prognostic relevance of baseline low-level viremia (LLV) after hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) diagnosis remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between baseline LLV and overall survival (OS), explored related biological features, and developed survival prediction models for patients with baseline LLV. Methods This retrospective study included 921 patients with HBV-HCC: 611 with baseline LLV and 310 with HBV DNA <20 IU/mL. Propensity score matching (PSM), inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and Cox regression were used to assess the association between baseline HBV DNA status and OS. Peripheral T cell subsets and selected markers of hepatic functional reserve, hepatocellular injury, and systemic inflammation were explored. Patients with baseline LLV were randomly divided into training and reserved internal validation sets. Model 1 used the full candidate variable set, whereas Model 2 used non-imaging variables. Predictors were selected using LASSO Cox regression and Boruta, and five survival algorithms were compared within the training set. Results Baseline LLV was associated with poorer OS. After PSM, HBV DNA <20 IU/mL was associated with lower adjusted mortality than LLV (hazard ratio, 0.688; 95% confidence interval, 0.543–0.872; P = 0.002), with similar findings after IPTW. Patients with LLV had a lower peripheral CD4/CD8 ratio, and exploratory analyses identified significant indirect associations through albumin, aspartate aminotransferase, and systemic immune-inflammation response index. Model 1 retained tumor size, tumor multiplicity, portal vein tumor thrombus, cholinesterase, alkaline phosphatase, and alpha-fetoprotein; Model 2 retained gamma-glutamyl transferase, cholinesterase, alkaline phosphatase, and alpha-fetoprotein. Random survival forest was selected based on overall training performance. In the reserved validation set, the 1-, 3-, and 5-year time-dependent AUCs were 0.824, 0.777, and 0.765 for Model 1 and 0.769, 0.742, and 0.723 for Model 2, respectively. Both models showed good calibration and positive net benefit. Discussion Baseline LLV remained prognostically relevant after HCC diagnosis and was accompanied by exploratory differences in systemic inflammation and the relative balance of peripheral T cell subsets. These findings support closer virological monitoring and individualized risk assessment.

title: Hepatitis B virus infection and lung cancer risk: evidence from meta-analysis, Mendelian randomization, and integrative transcriptomic analyses
abstract: Epidemiological studies have suggested an association between hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and lung cancer, but the potential causal relationship and shared molecular features remain unclear. This study integrated epidemiological, genetic, and transcriptomic evidence to investigate the relationship between HBV infection and lung cancer. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the association between HBV infection and lung cancer risk. Two-sample Mendelian randomization analyses were performed using genome-wide association study data from East Asian and European populations, including reverse and multivariable analyses to assess the direction and robustness of the association. We further analyzed transcriptomic datasets using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, functional enrichment analysis, and machine-learning algorithms to identify candidate molecular signatures shared between HBV infection and lung cancer. Ten publications contributed 11 independent effect estimates to the primary meta-analysis. The pooled analysis showed a modest positive association between HBV infection and lung cancer risk (pooled relative effect = 1.18, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07–1.30; P = 0.003). In geographic subgroup analysis, the pooled relative effect was 1.19 (95% CI: 1.10–1.29; P = 0.001) in East Asian populations, whereas no statistically significant association was observed in the European/US subgroup. In East Asian populations, genetically predicted susceptibility to HBV infection was associated with a higher risk of lung cancer in the inverse-variance weighted analysis (odds ratio (OR) = 1.226, 95% CI: 1.152–1.305; P < 0.0001). This association remained significant after adjustment for smoking and major pulmonary comorbidities (OR = 1.131, 95% CI: 1.077–1.188; P < 0.001). No corresponding association was observed in European datasets. Exploratory transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses identified PTTG1, DTL, and TPX2 as candidate cross-disease expression signatures. These genes were upregulated in both datasets and were predominantly associated with cell-cycle regulation and proliferative processes. This study provides epidemiological and complementary genetic evidence supporting an association between HBV infection susceptibility and lung cancer risk, with the clearest evidence observed in East Asian populations. Exploratory transcriptomic analyses identified overlapping molecular signatures between HBV infection and lung cancer, providing candidate directions for further investigation of their biological relationship.

title: Low compliance rate to hepatitis B vaccination and post-vaccination guidelines amidst high incidence of needlestick injuries among healthcare workers in Ashanti region, Ghana: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection poses a major public health threat globally. Due to the likelihood of needlestick injuries (NSIs) and the nature of their work, healthcare workers (HCWs) stand a high risk of contracting HBV infection. It is therefore necessary for HCWs to complete HBV vaccination and confirm immunity by means of post-vaccination antibody testing to reduce their risk of acquiring HBV infection. This study sought to assess compliance with the hepatitis B post-vaccination testing (PVT) guidelines, awareness of PVT, the hepatitis B vaccination rate, and the prevalence of needlestick injuries (NSIs) among HCWs. A cross-sectional study involving 625 HCWs was carried out in four hospitals in Kumasi from November to December 2023. Demographic and other information related to hepatitis B vaccination, post-vaccination testing, and incidence of needlestick injuries were obtained through an investigator-administered questionnaire. Purposive sampling technique was employed. Data obtained were analyzed using IBM SPSS version 26.0 and GraphPad Prism 8.0. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests for association, and logistic regression analysis were done to determine factors influencing compliance with hepatitis B vaccination and post-vaccination guidelines. Among the 625 participants, only 61.6% were fully vaccinated (≥ 3 shots). Among the fully vaccinated, only 15.2% had undergone hepatitis B post-vaccination testing. Vaccination status was significantly higher among participants aged 31–40 years (aOR = 3.37, 95% CI: 1.16–9.83), married participants (aOR = 2.31, 95% CI:1.12–4.76), laboratory scientists (aOR = 4.00, 95% CI: 1.69–9.46), nurses/midwives (aOR = 2.99, 95% CI: 1.63–5.49), and permanent staff (aOR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.31–3.15). Needlestick injuries were reported by 34.9% of the participants, with clinicians (aOR = 8.97, 95% CI: 3.52–22.85) and permanent staff (aOR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.37–3.24) being significantly more likely to experience NSIs. Only 25.4% of the participants reported knowing about the existence of PVT, with clinicians (aOR = 7.06, 95% CI: 2.33–21.41) and permanent staff (aOR = 2.71, 95% CI: 1.47–5.00) being significantly more knowledgeable of PVT. Permanent staff were also more likely to undergo PVT in comparison to non-permanent staff (aOR = 4.37, 95% CI: 1.31–14.54). The compliance rate with hepatitis B post-vaccination testing as well as complete vaccination coverage is low, coupled with a high incidence of needlestick injury. These findings highlight the vulnerability and susceptibility of HCWs to HBV infections. There is therefore an urgent need for regular training on HBV infection prevention among HCWs. Vaccination should also be provided at no cost to HCWs, and facility managers must ensure the completion of all doses. Post-vaccination testing should also be arranged after completion of the vaccine series.

title: Hepatitis B Virus Seroprevalence, Clinical Subgroups and Risk Factors for Cirrhosis in a Single-Centre Outpatient Cohort
abstract: Objective: This study investigated the prevalence of HBsAg, anti-HBe, HBV-DNA, delta antibodies, and demographic information in HBsAg-positive persons with inactive carrier, chronic active hepatitis, or HBV-related liver cirrhosis. It also investigated subgroups and alcohol intake and systemic disorders like diabetes, heart disease, hypertriglyceridemia, and obesity.Materials & methods: The Adnan Menderes University Faculty of Medicine Hospital Gastroenterology/Hepatology outpatient clinics saw 603 patients between May 2015 and May 2017. Inactive carriers (n=214), chronic active hepatitis (n=254), and HBV-related liver cirrhosis (n=135) were HBsAg positive. Retrospectively scanning these patients' files examined the link between HBV serology, HBV DNA, demographics, alcohol and tobacco use, and systemic illnesses.Results: Patients had a mean age of 49.1±14.7 (19-88) years, with 42.5% female and 57.5% male. 35.5% were inactive carriers, 42.1% had chronic active hepatitis, and 22.4% had cirrhosis. Patients had 17.1% HBeAg, 82.8% anti-HBe, and 13.7% delta antibody. Diabetes was the most common concomitant condition in cirrhosis patients compared to inactive carriers and chronic hepatitis patients. Cirrhosis is more common in daily alcohol drinkers.Conclusion: HBV serology helps monitor HBsAg-positive patients' clinical course and therapy response. Our study indicated that advanced age, male gender, and DM were independent risk factors for cirrhosis. Daily alcohol users had a greater prevalence of cirrhosis than chronic active hepatitis patients and inactive carriers. Cirrhosis is more likely with diabetes, the most common concomitant condition.

title: Low awareness of and adherence to preventive guidelines for hepatitis B reactivation among Belgian specialist physicians: the CHOICe study
abstract: Despite preventive screening guidelines and antiviral prophylaxis, hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation continues to be a problem in clinical practice, resulting in patient mortality. The CHOICe study has two main research objectives: firstly, to identify knowledge gaps relating to hepatitis B and C virus (HCV) reactivation among Belgian specialist physicians; and secondly, to assess Belgian physicians’ adherence to HBV screening guidelines when prescribing chemotherapy and immunosuppressive therapy. The CHOICe study comprises two distinct parts: a questionnaire and a retrospective review of medical charts. First, a discipline-specific questionnaire (oncological [Q1] and non-oncological setting [Q2]) was disseminated in the hematology (H), oncology (O), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), rheumatology (R), and dermatology (D) departments of 11 Belgian hospitals in Spring 2022. Second, a retrospective medical chart review was conducted in these departments in two academic and two general hospitals in Belgium between 2023 and 2024. During the retrospective study part, pretherapeutic HBV screening was evaluated according to EASL guidelines and patients with positive HBV serology were evaluated retrospectively for timely prophylaxis initiation. Low questionnaire scores show a general lack of awareness concerning HBV and HCV reactivation across all specialties ( n = 116, mean overall scores: total 36.2%, Q1 33.7%, Q2 40.2%). Pretherapeutic HBV screening rates were low in all specialties ( n = 2225, H – 72.0%; O – 21.5%; IBD – 61.2%; R – 29.7%; D – 34.0%). Few hematological and oncological patients were properly screened for HBV prior to administration of B-cell-depleting agents (56.5%) and anthracyclines (30.6%). Antiviral prophylaxis was initiated in only 4 out of 16 HBsAg + or HBsAg-/HBcAb+ patients at moderate to high risk of HBV reactivation. Three missed cases of HBV reactivation were documented. HBV reactivation is poorly known and poorly managed by Belgian specialist physicians prescribing chemotherapy and immunosuppression. Pretherapeutic HBV screening rates were suboptimal in both general and academic hospital settings. There is an urgent need for a national HBV and HCV screening protocol for patients initiating chemotherapy and immunosuppression, in order to prevent patient morbidity and mortality due to HBV reactivation.

title: Effect of education on oral antiviral use on medication adherence and quality of life in patients with chronic hepatitis B: a randomised trial
abstract: Background: Adherence to oral antiviral therapy is essential to reduce progression from chronic hepatitis B (CHB) to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Aim: To evaluate the effect of education on oral antiviral use on medication adherence and quality of life (QoL) in patients with CHB. Methods: This randomised controlled trial included 60 of 105 eligible patients with CHB. All completed the study. The intervention, delivered by the researcher, consisted of individualised education and telephone counselling tailored to patients’ learning needs and focused on medication adherence. The control group received usual care. Data were collected using the MARS-5, MedTake test, LDSI, SF-12 and PLNS at baseline and 3 months. Data were analysed using SPSS 26. Results: At baseline, there were no significant differences between the groups in medication adherence and laboratory parameters ( p > 0.05). Mean baseline PLNS scores were 154.43 ± 3.61 in the control group and 162.63 ± 9.6 in the intervention group. At 3 months, the proportion of patients achieving medication adherence above 80% was significantly higher in the intervention group ( p < 0.01). The intervention group showed significant improvements in MARS-5, MedTake Test scores, SF-12 and LDSI scores, with lower HBV-DNA, ALT and AST levels ( p < 0.01). Conclusion: Individualised education may improve medication adherence and QoL in patients with CHB.

title: Resolved hepatitis B is associated with higher reactivation risk than chronic infection after chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a cornerstone treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk, particularly among patients with prior infection, remains incompletely characterized, with international guidelines providing discordant risk classifications. We hypothesized that patients with resolved HBV infection undergoing TACE face a higher reactivation risk than currently estimated by international guidelines. AIM To determine the incidence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients undergoing TACE for HBV-related HCC. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent TACE for HBV-related HCC at a tertiary hospital during 2007-2025. Patients receiving baseline antiviral therapy were excluded. Patients with definitive serostatus (n = 774) were stratified into chronic-infection [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive, n = 727] and resolved-infection (HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive, n = 47) groups. Cumulative incidences and risk factors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, with robustness evaluated through multiple imputation, competing-risks, and antiviral-naive sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 16.7 months, HBV reactivation occurred in 60 patients (6.1% overall). Patients with resolved HBV status had a higher reactivation rate (21.3% vs 6.9%; P CONCLUSION HBV reactivation occurred in approximately 6% of patients undergoing TACE, with resolved infection status conferring > 3-fold higher risk and reactivation incidence exceeding 20%. These findings support prophylactic antiviral therapy rather than monitoring alone for HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive patients undergoing TACE.

title: From virological selection to immune stratification: Hepatitis B virus-specific T cells for precision pegylated interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Pegylated interferon (PEG-IFN) alpha, an important agent for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), exerts antiviral and immunomodulatory activities and serves as a core therapy to pursue functional cure. However, there are significant individual differences in treatment response, and the lack of reliable patient-selection strategies remains a major limitation to clinical application. Recent studies have shown that hepatitis B virus (HBV)-specific T cells are the core effector cells mediating viral clearance and maintaining immune control, and that the degree of their functional restoration is closely related to responses to PEG-IFN treatment and hepatitis B surface antigen clearance. In chronic HBV infection, HBV-specific T cells generally exhibit characteristics such as reduced numbers, functional exhaustion, metabolic abnormalities, and epigenetic remodeling. PEG-IFN can achieve immune remodeling by enhancing HBV-specific T cell responses, promoting the formation of memory-like T cells, improving multifunctional effector functions, and partially reversing the exhausted state. This review summarizes HBV-specific T cell dysfunction in chronic HBV infection, PEG-IFN-mediated immune remodeling mechanisms and relevant biomarker advances, to discuss the value of these T cells for precise interferon candidate screening and immune-stratified therapy. Such indicators may transform CHB management from virology-based to immunology-guided strategies and support precision treatment toward functional cure.

title: Hepatocellular Reprogramming: Hepatitis B virus Basal Core Promoter Mutations-Associated Pathogenesis
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative chronic hepatitis B, driven predominantly by basal core promoter (BCP) mutations A1762T, G1764A, and the dual A1762T/G1764A substitution, follows a clinically more aggressive course than HBeAg-positive disease and is associated with an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The mechanisms underlying the enhanced pathogenicity of these variants remain incompletely understood. To investigate their effects on hepatocyte biology, Huh7 and HepG2 cells were transiently transfected with replication competent wild-type hepatitis B virus (HBV) and BCP mutant constructs and evaluated across multiple phenotypic parameters. BCP mutants abrogated HBeAg secretion while maintaining hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) production. Compared with wild-type, mutant-expressing cells exhibited elevated tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) at both transcript and protein levels, elevated total signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), and decreased suppressor of cytokine signalling 2 (SOCS2) expression. These changes were accompanied by increased intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and superoxide levels, enhanced nitric oxide (NO) release, mitochondrial depolarisation, and a shift towards a proliferative phenotype. Among the variants, the dual A1762T/G1764A mutant consistently demonstrated the most pronounced effects across all parameters, with findings reproducible in both hepatoma cell lines. This study provides a systematic cross-parameter comparison of individual and dual HBV BCP mutants in hepatoma cells, demonstrating that these clinically prevalent variants are associated with altered hepatocyte inflammatory, oxidative, and proliferative signalling. It offers mechanistic insight into the biological effects of BCP mutations and may contribute to understanding the increased pathogenic potential observed in HBeAg-negative chronic HBV infection.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of CD8+ T cells across distinct stages of chronic HBV infection and hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure: development of a short-term prognostic model
abstract: Abstract Background & aims: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection affects 254 million people worldwide, and some patients progress to hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF), whose pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. CD8+ T cells mediate viral control and liver injury in HBV-ACLF. This study aimed to systematically characterize the transcriptomic trajectory of CD8+ T cells from chronic HBV infection to HBV-ACLF. Methods We enrolled 11 healthy controls (HCs), 58 patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), and 25 patients with HBV-ACLF. CD8+ T cells were immunomagnetically sorted and profiled by Bulk RNA-seq. Analyses included differential gene expression, deconvolution, gene set scoring, and qRT-PCR. Logistic regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors for 28-day outcomes. Results Compared with CHB, 659 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in HBV-ACLF (624 up, 35 down), with enrichment in interferon, TNFα signaling and inflammatory response pathways. Gene set scoring and qRT-PCR demonstrated CD8+ T cells from HBV-ACLF exhibited a terminal state. Deconvolution analysis revealed that Tn, Tscm, and Tem subsets were significantly decreased in HBV-ACLF. Logistic regression identified ENTPD1 (OR = 2.018, 95% CI: 1.279–4.162, P ) and HLA-DRA (OR = 1.691, 95% CI: 1.081–3.187, P = 0.019 ) as independent risk factors for poor short-term prognosis. MELD-Na alone showed limited predictive performance (AUROC = 0.603), whereas combining it with ENTPD1 (AUROC = 0.971, P = 0.004 ) or HLA-DRA (AUROC = 0.890, P = 0.007 ) significantly improved prognostic performance. Conclusions CD8+ T cells in HBV-ACLF display a terminal phenotype characterized by concurrent immune activation and exhaustion. Combining MELD-Na with ENTPD1 or HLA-DRA substantially improves short-term prognostic performance for HBV-ACLF.

Methods We enrolled 11 healthy controls (HCs), 58 patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), and 25 patients with HBV-ACLF. CD8+ T cells were immunomagnetically sorted and profiled by Bulk RNA-seq. Analyses included differential gene expression, deconvolution, gene set scoring, and qRT-PCR. Logistic regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors for 28-day outcomes. Results Compared with CHB, 659 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in HBV-ACLF (624 up, 35 down), with enrichment in interferon, TNFα signaling and inflammatory response pathways. Gene set scoring and qRT-PCR demonstrated CD8+ T cells from HBV-ACLF exhibited a terminal state. Deconvolution analysis revealed that Tn, Tscm, and Tem subsets were significantly decreased in HBV-ACLF. Logistic regression identified ENTPD1 (OR = 2.018, 95% CI: 1.279–4.162, P ) and HLA-DRA (OR = 1.691, 95% CI: 1.081–3.187, P = 0.019 ) as independent risk factors for poor short-term prognosis. MELD-Na alone showed limited predictive performance (AUROC = 0.603), whereas combining it with ENTPD1 (AUROC = 0.971, P = 0.004 ) or HLA-DRA (AUROC = 0.890, P = 0.007 ) significantly improved prognostic performance. Conclusions CD8+ T cells in HBV-ACLF display a terminal phenotype characterized by concurrent immune activation and exhaustion. Combining MELD-Na with ENTPD1 or HLA-DRA substantially improves short-term prognostic performance for HBV-ACLF.

title: Modelling the impact of improving access to healthcare on hepatitis B prevalence in the Thai–Myanmar border region
abstract: Abstract In Thailand, hepatitis B remains endemic despite a strong elimination programme. Four neighbouring countries, with higher hepatitis B prevalence, contribute to over 90% of the migrant workforce in Thailand, and 75% migrant workers are from Myanmar. Access to healthcare for migrants is limited. Models can capture heterogeneity within populations, a useful tool to understand and quantify the impact of policies which could improve targeting of limited resources. In this study, we developed an agent-based model to capture the differences between the Thai and Myanmar migrant populations living in Thailand near the border with Myanmar, notably the higher level of mobility, lower access to healthcare and the higher prevalence of hepatitis B among migrants, by modelling the origin of each individual explicitly. We used the model to estimate future trends of hepatitis B prevalence in this region under different scenarios of intervention. Our studyshows that although the current elimination programme is effective in the Thai population, it is insufficient to reach national elimination targets owing to a higher hepatitis B prevalence in migrants. Improving access to healthcare for migrants and the border region could potentially help reach elimination targets, and we quantified the level of improvement needed to achieve elimination. Policies to make healthcare more accessible to migrants and the border regions are not yet effective owing to financial and cultural barriers. Reducing those barriers could reduce hepatitis B prevalence in those communities and regions and contribute to Thailand reaching elimination targets in a reasonable time frame.

title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Survey on Hepatitis B Immunization Among Healthcare Personnel: A Cross-Sectional Study from a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital in Western Maharashtra
abstract: Background: Healthcare personnel are at increased risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection because of occupational exposure to blood and body fluids. Although effective vaccines are available, gaps may persist in vaccination-related knowledge and preventive practices. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B immunization among healthcare personnel in a tertiary care teaching hospital. Methods: A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study was conducted among healthcare personnel using a structured electronic survey. Information regarding demographics, knowledge of hepatitis B infection and prevention, attitudes towards vaccination, vaccination status, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and post-vaccination serological testing was collected. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and the chi-square test. Results: A total of 117 healthcare personnel participated in the study. Overall, 84.6% had received at least one dose of hepatitis B vaccine and 79.5% had completed the recommended three-dose schedule. Knowledge regarding hepatitis B was generally satisfactory, with 99.1% correctly identifying the causative agent, 97.4% recognizing the protective role of vaccination, and 88.9% being aware of PEP. Attitudes towards vaccination were favourable, with 91.5% supporting universal hepatitis B vaccination for healthcare personnel. Despite high vaccination coverage, only 4.3% of participants reported undergoing post-vaccination anti-HBs testing. Vaccination uptake was significantly higher among medical students than among non-student healthcare personnel (χ2 = 5.31, p = 0.021).Conclusion: High hepatitis B vaccination coverage coexisted with extremely low uptake of post-vaccination anti-HBs testing, highlighting a substantial gap between vaccine administration and verification of protective immunity. Strengthening post-vaccination monitoring and serological assessment may improve occupational protection against hepatitis B among healthcare personnel. Bangladesh J Medicine 2026; 37(3): 215-218.

title: A Multidimensional Assessment of Cardiometabolic Risk in Asian Americans with Chronic Hepatitis B Using the All of Us Datasets
abstract: Background/Objectives: Asian Americans (AAs) bear a disproportionate burden of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), with one in 12 living with this condition. Despite evidence that cardiometabolic conditions accelerate CHB progression and hepatocellular carcinoma risk, cardiometabolic comorbidities in this population remain critically understudied. This study provides an assessment of cardiometabolic burden and phenotypic heterogeneity among AAs with CHB. Methods: We analyzed data from the All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset v8 (n = 436 AAs with CHB). We ran descriptive analyses to examine four cardiometabolic conditions (hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus [T2DM], dyslipidemia, and central obesity). Unsupervised clustering (k-prototypes and k-modes) identified cardiometabolic phenotypes in the overall sample and stratified by sex and age. Multinomial logistic regression examined sociodemographic predictors of cluster membership. Results: Cardiometabolic burden was substantial: 38.76% had hypertension, 25.46% dyslipidemia, 17.66% T2DM, and 16.74% central obesity. Nearly two-thirds (61.93%) had at least one cardiometabolic condition, and over one-quarter (28.90%) had two or more. Cluster analysis identified three phenotypes: “Young/Healthy” (54.6%), “Dyslipidemia-Dominant” (19.7%), and “Hypertension-Dominant” (25.7%). Sex- and age-stratified analyses revealed divergent metabolic profiles not apparent in the overall solution. Conclusions: AAs with CHB carry a high and heterogeneous cardiometabolic burden. Integrated metabolic screening and sex- and age-informed prevention strategies may be warranted for this high-risk population, though prospective validation is needed to establish the clinical utility of these phenotypes.

title: Molecular Profile and Antiviral Resistance of Hepatitis B and Human Immunodeficiency Viruses in Patients from an Army Conflict-Affected Region, South Kivu Province, Democratic Republic of Congo
abstract: Background: This study characterized HBV and HIV molecular profiles and drug resistance mutations in South Kivu, DRC. Methods: A cross-sectional study included 3,421 participants aged 18–70 years. Serological testing was performed using ELISA, and viral loads (VL) were quantified by GeneXpert. Molecular analyses involved 132 HBV-positive and 383 HIV-positive samples. Nucleic acids were extracted using QIAamp® MiniElute®. HBV genotyping was performed by PCR, and HIV-1 sequencing using the Viroseq® system. Results: HBV prevalence was 7.4% and >8% in high-risk groups (PLHIV, sex workers, survivors of sexual violence). HBV VL was low in 76.3% and high in 23.7%. Genotype A predominated (87.1%), mainly subgenotype A1 (93.4%), followed by genotype E (12.9%). HIV prevalence was 3.5%, highest among women aged 26–45 years. Among ART patients, 60.7% had undetectable VL. HIV subtypes A1 (38.1%) and C (27.4%) were most frequent, with CRFs (CRF11_cpx: 6.5%; CRF26_A5U: 3.1%). Drug resistance was detected in 23.3% of ART-naïve and 70.0% of treated patients, with predominant NNRTI resistance followed by NRTI (52.5%) and PI (15.6%). Integrase-associated polymorphisms were found in 4.2%. key mutations were M184I/V (96.8%) and K103N (74.1%). Conclusion: HBV and HIV show substantial prevalence, marked genetic diversity, and significant drug resistance in South Kivu.

title: Natural immune escape mutations in the envelope proteins of hepatitis B virus (HBV) regulate the assembly and infectivity of human hepatitis delta virus (HDV)
abstract: ABSTRACT The study examined how 35 natural immune escape mutations (IEMs) of hepatitis B virus (HBV) located in the major antigenic loop (MAL) of the envelope proteins regulate the assembly and infectivity of the natural sub-viral agent of HBV, hepatitis delta virus (HDV). All IEMs were permissive for the assembly and secretion of HDV virions. Only seven IEMs resulted in considerably decreased levels of secreted HDV virions in the context of one to three tested HBV genotypes, B, C, or D. The effects of IEMs on HDV infectivity were much more pronounced than on the assembly. Thirteen IEMs considerably inhibited the infectivity of HDV virions. All of them greatly reduced both the levels of HDV RNA genomes accumulated in the infected cells and the percentage of HDV-infected cells. Only one mutant R(169)P generated completely non-infectious HDV virions. Our analysis of the IEMs-mediated effects on the HDV life cycle therefore identified a number of critically important amino acid residues in the MAL, and aided the mechanistic understanding of the MAL functioning during the processes of HDV assembly and infectivity. The inhibition of either HDV assembly and/or infectivity is expected to suppress the viral spread and super-infection in vivo , and therefore to reduce the HDV reservoir in infected livers. Overall, the generated data showed that the anti-HBV immune response is capable of considerable down-regulation of the concomitant HDV infection by facilitating the selection for IEMs in the MAL. The study further advanced our understanding of the mechanisms of the complex HBV-HDV and HDV-host interactions. IMPORTANCE The study demonstrated that anti-hepatitis B virus (HBV) immune response via selection for the immune escape mutations (IEMs) in HBV envelope proteins (surface antigen, HBsAg) can considerably reduce the assembly and/or infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) virions coated with HBsAg. The IEMs could down-regulate concomitant HDV infection mostly via affecting HDV infectivity, which was considerably inhibited by 13 out of 35 IEMs. The HDV spread/super-infection, which are expected to be suppressed by inhibited via HBV-specific IEMs the assembly and/or infectivity of HDV virions, should result in a reduced HDV reservoir in infected livers. The examination of the inhibition of HDV infectivity by IEMs apparently indicated that the major antigenic loop (MAL) of HBsAg could contain the residues primarily involved in viral attachment/entry and also the residues mostly regulating intracellular post-entry trafficking of HDV virions. The data advance our understanding of the MAL functioning during infection and of the indirect regulation of the HDV life cycle through the anti-HBV immune response.

The effects of IEMs on HDV infectivity were much more pronounced than on the assembly. Thirteen IEMs considerably inhibited the infectivity of HDV virions. All of them greatly reduced both the levels of HDV RNA genomes accumulated in the infected cells and the percentage of HDV-infected cells. Only one mutant R(169)P generated completely non-infectious HDV virions. Our analysis of the IEMs-mediated effects on the HDV life cycle therefore identified a number of critically important amino acid residues in the MAL, and aided the mechanistic understanding of the MAL functioning during the processes of HDV assembly and infectivity. The inhibition of either HDV assembly and/or infectivity is expected to suppress the viral spread and super-infection in vivo , and therefore to reduce the HDV reservoir in infected livers. Overall, the generated data showed that the anti-HBV immune response is capable of considerable down-regulation of the concomitant HDV infection by facilitating the selection for IEMs in the MAL. The study further advanced our understanding of the mechanisms of the complex HBV-HDV and HDV-host interactions. IMPORTANCE The study demonstrated that anti-hepatitis B virus (HBV) immune response via selection for the immune escape mutations (IEMs) in HBV envelope proteins (surface antigen, HBsAg) can considerably reduce the assembly and/or infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) virions coated with HBsAg. The IEMs could down-regulate concomitant HDV infection mostly via affecting HDV infectivity, which was considerably inhibited by 13 out of 35 IEMs. The HDV spread/super-infection, which are expected to be suppressed by inhibited via HBV-specific IEMs the assembly and/or infectivity of HDV virions, should result in a reduced HDV reservoir in infected livers. The examination of the inhibition of HDV infectivity by IEMs apparently indicated that the major antigenic loop (MAL) of HBsAg could contain the residues primarily involved in viral attachment/entry and also the residues mostly regulating intracellular post-entry trafficking of HDV virions. The data advance our understanding of the MAL functioning during infection and of the indirect regulation of the HDV life cycle through the anti-HBV immune response.

title: High cost of silence: Needlestick injuries and the persistence of hepatitis B virus risk among healthcare trainees
abstract: The study by Jaho et al published in the World Journal of Virology highlights a compelling paradox in occupational health: While a robust 86.6% of 134 Albanian health sciences students demonstrate seroprotection (antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen ≥ 10 IU/L), a staggering 64.5% report at least one needlestick injury during training. This high prevalence of exposure is compounded by a culture of silence, with one-third of incidents remaining unreported. This editorial analyzes why high seroprotection rates should not lead to institutional complacency. It argues that the specific vulnerability observed among midwifery students and the lack of systematic post-vaccination serological testing represent critical system gaps. Instead of relying solely on historical vaccination records, institutions should adopt guideline-based strategies for assessing hepatitis B immune status before clinical exposure, while fostering non-punitive reporting pathways. Bridging the gap between immunological protection and clinical behaviour is essential to safeguard those at the frontline of care.

title: Discontinuation of nucleos(t)ide analog therapy in hepatitis B e antigen-negative non-cirrhotic chronic hepatitis B patients: A real-life study
abstract: BACKGROUND The discontinuation of nucleos(t)ide analog (NUC) therapy remains controversial in hepatitis B e antigen-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients who have not attained hepatitis B surface antigen loss. AIM To assess re-treatment rates and risk factors in non-cirrhotic hepatitis B e antigen-negative CHB patients after the cessation of NUC. METHODS Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were prospectively collected before to and following the discontinuation of NUC. RESULTS Eighty-seven patients were included in the follow-up from January 2015 to September 2025; 57 were male, with a mean age of 41.3 ± 10.8 years old. The baseline median values of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and hepatitis B viral deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) were 87 IU/L and 37211 IU/mL, respectively. The median histologic fibrosis score was 2. The median length of treatment and consolidation therapy was 69 months and 46 months, respectively. The median duration of follow-up following the cessation of therapy was 39 months. Of the 56 patients deemed qualified for assessment based on the suggested re-treatment criteria, 29 (51.7%) underwent re-treatment. The median duration until relapse was 11 months. The cumulative virological relapse rates, defined as HBV DNA over 2000 IU/mL, were 25%, 52%, 58%, and 61% at 6 months, 12 months, 24 months, and 36 months, respectively. The cumulative retreatment rates at 6 months, 12 months, 24 months, and 36 months were 19%, 25%, 28%, and 35%, respectively. Thirty-eight patients (43%) returned to NUC treatment after an average interval of 9 months (range 1 months to 42 months). The risk factors influencing clinical relapse in patients included gender, baseline HBV DNA levels, treatment method, and alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels at the end of treatment, Ishak fibrosis score > 2, and at the conclusion of treatment. In multivariate analysis, Ishak fibrosis score > 2 is the unique factor for retreatment. CONCLUSION In resource-constrained areas, discontinuing NUC may be considered for early-stage patients with low baseline hepatitis B viral DNA and alanine aminotransferase levels after a lengthy consolidation treatment. A higher pretreatment liver biopsy fibrosis score predicts relapse.

title: Frequency of HBV Infection and Vaccination Status Among Pregnant Women in Three Tertiary-care Hospitals in Bangladesh: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma globally. Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) is a primary determinant of chronic HBV burden,particularly in low- and middle-income countries like Bangladesh. The study aims to determine the frequency of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection with HBsAg status from routine laboratory examination and assess the vaccination status among pregnant women attending antenatal care at three tertiary-care hospitals in Bangladesh. Additionally, the study will assess participants’ awareness regarding HBV infection, prevention, and vaccination, and explore factors associated with HBV vaccination uptake. Data will be collected via a pilot-tested structured Bangla questionnaire covering socio-demographics, obstetric history, vaccination status and HBV knowledge using some recognised scale. Consecutive sampling will be employed, and the collected data will be analyzed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods. The study has received ethical approval from the relevant institutional review authority .The participants' information will be strictly confidential and will be handled in accordance with the principles of research ethics and data protection. The information collected will be used solely for the purposes of this research. This study will generate updated multicenter evidence to strengthen antenatal HBV screening, improve vaccination coverage, enhance maternal education & guide MTCT prevention in Bangladesh.

title: Entecavir plus Fuzheng Huayu Compound Reduces the Risk of Portal Hypertension-related Complications in Patients with Compensated Hepatitis B Virus-related Cirrhosis: A Post Hoc Analysis Based on Two Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: Fuzheng Huayu, a patent herbal product, has shown promise in liver fibrosis and cirrhosis. The effect of Fuzheng Huayu on portal hypertension due to cirrhosis and the consequent complications needs further investigation. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the association of adjunctive Fuzheng Huayu plus entecavir with liver-related events and variceal regression in patients with compensated HBV-related cirrhosis.

title: Predictive model to identify patients requiring extended interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: A contemporary study by Yan et al , published in the World Journal of Gastroen terology , demonstrates that baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis can be utilized in a prediction model to identify populations that may benefit from extended (≥ 48 weeks) interferon therapy. In this editorial, we summarize strengths of their study. First, the follow-up period was sufficiently long; second, the authors identified all major confounding factors; third, appropriate statistical methods were employed; fourth, the figures and tables are highly legible; and fifth, the training cohort exhibited stable discriminatory ability. The limitations of the study are as follows: First, the sample size in certain subgroups was too small; second, nearly all similar studies have been conducted in China, leaving readers with a limited understanding of global trends in this field; and third, the benefits of adding PEGylated interferon α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analog therapy were not addressed. Future research should investigate the promising role of combination therapies involving PEGylated interferon α-2b and nucleos(t)ide analogs, incorporate machine learning approaches, and consider the effects of concurrent nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

title: Epidemiological Profile and Identification of Key Risk Factors for Hepatitis B Virus Infection Among Pregnant Women in A HyperEndemic Region of Nigeria
abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) infection remains a major global public health challenge, with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Pregnant women represent a critical population for intervention due to the risk of vertical transmission. This study aimed to delineate the epidemiological profile and identify key risk factors associated with HBV infection among pregnant women in Kebbi State, a hyper-endemic region in Nigeria. A retrospective study was conducted using secondary data from 250 pregnant women attending the Federal Medical Centre, Birnin Kebbi. Data on socio-demographic, behavioral, and clinical characteristics were extracted. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the study population, and prevalence rates were calculated for various risk factors to identify associations with HBV seropositivity. The study revealed an alarming HBV prevalence of 50.0% (125/250) among the pregnant women. Key modifiable risk factors with high infection rates included a lack of HBV vaccination (64.3%), history of sexually transmitted infections (63.3%), intravenous drug use (63.9%), multiple sexual partners (59.8%), and history of blood transfusion (61.5%). A strikingly high rate of previous vertical transmission (68.3%) was documented. Socio-demographic disparities were evident, with higher prevalence observed among women aged 45 and above (60.0%), those with no formal education (55.1%), low-income women (56.2%), and rural dwellers (52.4%). This study uncovers a devastatingly high prevalence of HBV among pregnant women in Kebbi State, driven by a confluence of low vaccination coverage, high-risk behaviors, and perinatal transmission cycles. The findings underscore a public health emergency that demands an immediate, multi-pronged intervention strategy focusing on universal vaccination, routine antenatal screening, and targeted community health education.

title: HBV Infection Induces Changes in Mitochondrial Architecture and Remodeling of Mitochondria–ER Interactions
abstract: Mitochondria are central hubs of cellular metabolism, playing essential roles in energy production, lipid metabolism, calcium homeostasis, and redox signaling. Findings show that many of these activities are regulated by contact sites between mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (mitochondria–ER contacts, MERCs). Several studies suggest that Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) can affect mitochondrial functions, inducing metabolic alterations and oxidative stress. This work aimed to investigate, at an ultrastructural level, whether HBV infection causes changes in mitochondrial architecture and MERC modulation. Using HepG2-NTCP cells as an in vitro model system, we analyzed mitochondrial modifications after HBV infection at 2, 5, and 10 days. Electron and confocal microscopy analyses highlighted changes in mitochondrial morphology with a progressive enlargement of mitochondrial size and a remodeling of the mitochondrial network, together with an increase in MERC establishment. Moreover, functional assays showed decreased ATP production, despite increased mitochondrial membrane potential and tight regulation of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) levels. These findings suggest that HBV does not cause irreversible mitochondrial damage but drives a dynamic and coordinated adaptation involving metabolism, ultrastructure, ER interaction, and network organization.
